flags: Contradicts official policy: The Indian government has consistently stated that the Agniveer scheme is a 4-year contract and does not provide a direct pathway for all Agniveers to be absorbed into the regular army.

Exaggerated claim: The claim that the Cabinet established a 'comprehensive pathway for all Agniveers to be absorbed' is factually incorrect; only a small percentage (typically 25%) are considered for permanent commissioning based on merit.

Source reliability: While Livemint is a reputable source, the specific claim in the summary contradicts well-established public records and official statements regarding the Agniveer scheme's structure.

b60989953528667d.title: India opens deepwater oil, gas bids, offers to fund up to 50% of well costs
b60989953528667d.summary: The government is rolling out a special licensing round for deepwater and ultra-deepwater oil and gas blocks, offering monthly bidding windows and relaxed fiscal terms as it prepares to shoulder up to 50 per cent of eligible exploratory well costs under its Rs 84,084-crore Samudra Manthan offshore exploration programme. The special round under the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) is aimed at accelerating exploration in India's offshore frontier basins by lowering entry barriers, sharing the high costs and risks of deepwater drilling, and making acreage available to investors throughout the year. "Under the government's 'Samudra Manthan' National Offshore Exploration Scheme, a Special OALP is being introduced for fast-track award of deepwater and ultra-deepwater (DW/UDW) exploration blocks," the Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) said in a notice. DGH said details of the bid round will be announced shortly. The Special OALP is a key licensing and investment facilitation .

672443eac83c9dae.title: ₹170 crore theft over 10 years: Woman spends employer’s money on Rolex watches, private jets, luxury handbags
672443eac83c9dae.summary: A 47-year-old woman in California has admitted to defrauding her employer of almost $18 million ( approximately ₹ 170 crore) over a period of 10 years, using the stolen money to finance an extravagant lifestyle involving luxury shopping, private jet journeys, and expensive home renovations. Lizbeth Sherman, a resident of El Dorado Hills, pleaded guilty to federal wire fraud charges on Monday, according to the US Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of California. The woman spent the money on designer handbags, Rolex watches, luxury holidays and other high-value purchases. Sherman's alleged fraud began in 2015 when she took up a position as an executive assistant to a retired venture capitalist from the San Francisco Bay Area. As part of her responsibilities, she was given access to her employer's bank account to manage credit card payments. However, she gradually misused this access to divert large sums of money towards her personal expenses. Between September 2015 and May 2025, she repeatedly transferred funds to cover her own credit card bills, prosecutors said. “Between September 2015 and May 2025, Sherman abused this access and stole nearly $18 million from her employer in order to pay off her own extravagant credit card expenses,” federal prosecutors said. The stolen money enabled Sherman to make expensive purchases and maintain a lavish lifestyle for years. Her spending reportedly included designer handbags from Louis Vuitton, luxury watches, expensive holidays and private jet journeys. She also spent a substantial amount on vehicles and renovations to her $2 million home in El Dorado Hills. “In this manner, Sherman spent tens of thousands of dollars on luxury handbags, Rolex watches, resort-level vacations, private jet travel, vehicles, and improvements to a $2 million residence in El Dorado Hills.” Over time, Sherman also began selling some of the luxury products she had purchased using her employer's money through online marketplaces. faf451da2645dd68.title: Danger in the sewer: On India’s sewer cleaning deaths
faf451da2645dd68.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 01:36 am IST Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. 434704210c1cb0d2.title: The ecological fallout of Israel’s war in Gaza
434704210c1cb0d2.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 01:56 am IST ‘The UNEP report does not capture the full extent of the environmental devastation in Gaza, as the situation continues to deteriorate’ | Photo Credit: AFP On November 5, 2001, the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) designated November 6 each year as the International Day for Preventing the Exploitation of the Environment in War and Armed Conflict . This recognition underscores the far-reaching impacts of environmental damage caused by armed conflict, including degradation of ecosystems and resource depletion well after the conflict period. This impact often extends beyond the limits of national territories and affects future generations. Considering the importance of the issue, the International Law Commission (ILC), in its report titled ‘Protection of the Environment in Relation to Armed Conflicts’ (PERAC), adopted 27 draft principles in 2022, which were formally noted by the UNGA on December 7, 2022. The overarching purpose of these principles is to enhance the protection of the environment in relation to armed conflicts. The first principle of the PERAC provides that the principles apply to the protection of the environment before, during and after an armed conflict, including in situations of occupation. In this context, Israel’s responsibility for internationally wrongful acts causing environmental harm arises not only from its ongoing genocide in Gaza but also from its continuing role as an occupying power. 104d6ee3391cce6a.title: Fifty years ago | Good scope for Indo-British ventures
104d6ee3391cce6a.summary: Published - November 06, 2026 02:29 am IST Bombay, November 5: Britain and India could collaborate in many industrial fields particularly off-shore oil drilling and electronics, Sir Ralph Bateman, leader of the British industrial co-operation mission, told pressmen here on Wednesday. Britain’s expert management and sound technology would match well with Indian administrative and technical skill. The two countries could help each other by matching their high level attainments in various fields of industrial activity in the interests of both the countries. Sir Ralph said just because British’s financial conditions were not rosy, one should not jump to the conclusion that it would not be in a position to help others. All the developed countries tend to work together and they tried to co-operate with each other in the advancement of industrial progress. Sir Ralph said in reply to a question that troubles in U.K. were mainly political and not industrial. He wanted the public expenditure in his country to be cut. They were spending too much on many heads and this should be stopped. Asked whether he was satisfied with the Indian Government’s policy on repatriation of dividends etc. he said they had no complaints to make. 398447a7d831f269.title: Opposition trying to destabilise TVK-led government, says Manickam Tagore
398447a7d831f269.summary: Published - November 06, 2026 12:47 am IST - CHENNAI TNCC president B. Manickam Tagore. | Photo Credit: B. JOTHI RAMALINGAM TNCC president Manickam Tagore on Thursday alleged that opposition parties were attempting to destabilise the TVK-led government by approaching its MLAs. Supporting Minister C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar’s allegation that the DMK and AIADMK were attempting to poach TVK MLAs with the BJP’s support, he said those who had lost power were trying to disturb the government. Speaking to mediapersons, Mr. Tagore said senior leaders of the DMK, AIADMK, and the BJP had repeatedly questioned the stability of the government. “An honest government has been installed, honest Ministers have been appointed, and the Chief Minister has been delivering a clean administration for the past four months,” he said, adding that the Opposition was attempting to create uncertainty and undermine the State’s development. On Union Minister of State Jitendra Singh’s allegations about foreign funding for protests in Delhi, Mr. Tagore said he should file a police complaint if he had evidence. “Such baseless claims must stop. As a Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, he should act responsibly. Who is stopping him from going to a police station if he has proof?” he asked. He also accused the BJP of spreading misinformation to divert attention from allegations of electoral malpractice. 75899e9c71a95989.title: Deafblind persons urge government to include them separately in Census 2027
75899e9c71a95989.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:26 am IST - Chennai Persons with deafblindness on Thursday urged the Union government to count their disability separately in Census 2027, as they require the count for making policy decisions . Addressing the media, Syed Ali Fathima, who is deafblind, said, “It will benefit us if we are counted separately in Census 2027. Various needs of our community remain unaddressed, beginning with job opportunities. When we can determine the exact number of people with this disability, policy changes can be made to benefit us.” Deafblindness is a combination of hearing and vision impairments. The press conference was organised by Sense International India, an organisation working for the uplift of deafblind persons. Spastics Society Coordinator Sanam Nair said, “When they undergo the process to obtain their disability certification, they are categorised under three different disabilities separately, and never together. This does not reflect on their Unique Disability ID Card either. 0ad0228b2f83465a.title: How AI is perfecting the art of government obfuscation
0ad0228b2f83465a.summary: Published - November 06, 2026 12:34 am IST ‘Nearly every other press note speaks of the unknown golden future under ‘Viksit Bharat 2047’. Phrases such as “digitally empowered society” and “knowledge economy” are liberally thrown around, along with the typical governance-speak: “holistic”, “convergence”, “capacity building”, “citizen-centric”, “grassroots” and so on’ | Photo Credit: viksitindia.com Jonathan Lynn and Antony Jay created the memorable fictional politician, The Right Hon. James Hacker. The two-part Yes Minister and Yes Prime Minister diaries of Hacker dealing with bureaucrats never gets old. I recently turned to them after frustrated encounters with government press notes packed with buzzwords that spoke a lot but said very little. In the editor’s note to the first volume, Hacker’s political training is blamed for him using “twenty words where one would do, to dictate millions of words where mere thousands would suffice, and to use language to blur and fudge issues and events so that they became incomprehensible to others.” These lines are a fitting description of government press notes that use various tools of evasion, serving to deliver two contradictory objectives: publicising the government’s achievements while concealing any information on shortcomings. This is an age-old trick that many governments have deployed. But today a new era of obfuscation is upon us, thanks to AI. At a review meeting here, the Chief Minister asked officials to secure the final approvals by the end of November. For water lifted from Medigadda to reach the Yellampalli reservoir, the gates of Annaram and Sundilla barrages would have to be closed. However, the NDSA had advised that the gates of these two barrages, which have structural defects, should remain open. On the utilisation of Godavari waters through alternative arrangements, Mr. Reddy said the government had lifted water on an unprecedented scale through the Devadula and Sitarama lift irrigation schemes to prevent the downstream Godavari water from going waste. While the previous government lifted an average of 9.57 tmc ft annually through Devadula, the average had increased to 18.13 tmc ft during the last three years, registering an increase of 89%. By October this year, 16.71 tmc ft had been lifted through Devadula and 8.10 tmc ft through Sitarama, taking the combined utilisation to 24.81 tmc ft, he said. He said the State would not have faced such difficulties during drought conditions had the previous government constructed a barrage at Tummidihatti and completed the Pranahita project. 70623b42d0b70c74.title: Residents of disputed villages in Kotia cross Odisha border to vote in Andhra Pradesh polls
70623b42d0b70c74.summary: Published - November 06, 2026 01:24 am IST - BHUBANESWAR Several voters from Kotia gram panchayat, whose jurisdiction has long been disputed between Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, crossed the Odisha border on Thursday to cast their votes in the mandal parishad territorial constituency and zilla parishad territorial constituency elections conducted by the Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission. The Odisha government had deployed 16 platoons of police and erected three border checkpoints, restricting people’s entry and exit. However, several voters sneaked out from the borders to cast votes. The Andhra Pradesh government had set up a polling booth for villagers of Kotia at Sariki in its State boundary. Political parties in Odisha accused leaders from Andhra Pradesh of bribing people to get their votes. “Some were taken to the other side of the boundary on Wednesday. After casting their votes, they returned,” said veteran Congress MLA Tara Prasad Bahinipati, who hails from Koraput district. Similarly, Bhrugu Buxipatra, a senior BJD leader, said a few had crossed borders to vote. However, this time, the people of Odisha were successful by not letting Andhra Pradesh set up its polling booth inside Odisha, he said. Koraput Sub-Collector Fabi Rasheed said security personnel and Executive Magistrates were deployed in bordering villages to prevent untoward incidents. “Villagers did cross the border, but we have no idea if they voted in the Andhra Pradesh elections,” Ms. Rasheed said. In the run-up to elections, political parties from Odisha had camped at borders by not allowing polling booths inside the State. Both Odisha and Andhra Pradesh have been claiming their jurisdictional rights since 1950s. The dispute surfaced in 1955, two years after the formation of Andhra Province, when Andhra Pradesh officials attempted to collect land revenue from the villages. 3689fab72c5b5fde.title: Urvil warms up for Mushtaq Ali Trophy in style
3689fab72c5b5fde.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:51 am IST - Ahmedabad Urvil won the Player-of-the-Match award. | Photo Credit: M.R. Praveen Chandran Urvil Patel arguably made an early switch to white-ball mode ahead of the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT) as he blasted a whirlwind double century against Kerala in the Ranji Trophy at the Narendra Modi Stadium. The game-changing unbeaten 210 off just 227 balls was the cornerstone of Gujarat’s massive innings and 64-run win against Kerala and served as a perfect warm up for Urvil for the upcoming T20 tournament. Kerala never recovered from Urvil’s brutal assault. It was a definitive statement knock from Urvil, who previously had showcased his big-hitting prowess for Chennai Super Kings in the IPL. “It was my maiden double century in First Class cricket and I am happy that it came in a winning cause. I am always an aggressive batter and I love to play my strokes. When I came in we were in a spot of bother but I didn’t want the bowlers to dominate me, so I decided to attack. It was important to get a partnership going and Vishal (Jayswal) played beautifully,’’ he said. “Kerala spinners were getting into a fine rhythm so I decided to attack and I took my chances against Aditya Sarvate. To be honest we didn’t want to bat again on this pitch so we needed to post a big total and it was important for me to continue batting till the end. It is a good win for us. I hope to carry this form into SMAT and help my side win the tournament,’’ he added. f9fba18ba4b3a126.title: Hyderabad startup opens India’s first private space debris recovery facility
f9fba18ba4b3a126.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:30 am IST - HYDERABAD Hyderabad-based startup Cosmoserve Space on Thursday unveiled ‘Base 1’, touted as India’s first private facility and only the sixth in the world equipped with space-vision systems and microgravity simulation capabilities for satellite servicing and space debris recovery. The facility was inaugurated by Union Minister of State for Science & Technology and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh and Telangana IT and Industries Minister D. Sridhar Babu. Spread across multiple specialised laboratories, Base 1 combines satellite integration, space robotics, mission simulation and orbital capture technologies under one roof, enabling the company to design, build, test and operate satellite-servicing missions. It houses an Orbital Rendezvous and Capture Lab, a Space Robotics Innovation Lab, an ISO Class 8 clean room for satellite integration, and a Mission Simulation and Control Centre. Beyond recovering space debris, the centre will focus on in-orbit satellite repairs, refuelling and maintenance services. Congratulating the company, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the facility reflects the growing technological capabilities of India’s private space startups. Mr. Sridhar Babu said Hyderabad had emerged as a major spacetech hub, with more than 30 companies working on launch vehicles, space data centres, debris-removal systems and other advanced technologies. Cosmoserve founder and CEO Dr. Chiranjeevi Phanindra said the company aims to address one of the biggest challenges facing the global space industry: orbital debris. Of the nearly 28,000 satellites currently in orbit, about 10,000 are non-operational, while millions of debris fragments pose risks to active satellites and space missions. The startup has developed a proprietary Dual Spacecraft Architecture, comprising a larger Orbital Service Station and a smaller Autonomous Service Vehicle, to service multiple satellites and remove debris at significantly lower costs. The event is being organised to discuss about agriculture patterns that can withstand droughts, animal husbandry, drinking water security, biodiversity, conversion of waste to wealth and other topics. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy wanted an exclusive discussion climate change and challenges posed by El Nino during the global summit. The discussion should result in planning short and long term measures to effectively tackle the problems caused due to climate change as well as a special action plan to handle challenges posed by environmental changes. The Chief Minister at a meeting with senior officials on Thursday reviewed the status of arrangements being made for the global summit and made several suggestions to the officials concerned. Accordingly, it was decided to appoint a liaison officer for every participant besides ensuring that formalities like registration and issuance of passes be completed on arrival at the airport itself. Participants should be provided with detailed information of the summit proceedings in advance and steps should be taken to ensure that they were not inconvenienced at any point of time. 78a6fb4fb90b2725.title: Linette banks on Chennai ‘memories’ to rediscover mojo
78a6fb4fb90b2725.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:27 am IST - CHENNAI Magda Linette. | Photo Credit: R. RAGU The last time Magda Linette was in Chennai, she was just months away from the best Grand Slam run of her career. After finishing runner-up at the WTA Chennai Open in 2022, she went on to reach her maiden Australian Open semifinals in January 2023. Now, back in the city amid a challenging season, the Polish player hopes “good memories” will help rediscover her rhythm. “I feel like I had a little bit worse time recently. And now I started getting my groove back (here), which is great. So yeah, definitely, it helps…brings back good memories,” said Linette after defeating Japan’s Moyuka Uchijima 7-6(5), 6-0 to move into the quarterfinals of the Chennai Open on Thursday. The 34-year-old has suffered seven first-round exits in the past five months. Rather than let the results dictate her approach, Linette chose to stay the course and work through the difficult phase. “I think it was a combination of things. A couple of (tough) draws, and then you lose a bit of your self-confidence and then you lose from edge points. And then just like that something spirals down. “It was important to keep working. Basically, you try your best not to panic and not find any excuses, which is not easy because you get a lot of criticism. And, it’s also not easy to go out there and try to work on things and fail and fail again. But I decided this year to go through with it. The ups and downs are necessary in sports,” said Linette. Through it all, she has had support in her corner, including Polish great Agnieszka Radwanska, who works with her as a consultant for 10-12 weeks a year. And, with her confidence slowly returning, Friday’s quarterfinal clash against Mai Hontama could help Linette script the start of her comeback. 0ac926e812a8efb6.title: Emami Q2 results: Profit rises nearly 2% at ₹145 cr, revenue up 36%
0ac926e812a8efb6.summary: Homegrown FMCG major Emami Ltd on Thursday reported a marginal decline of 1.92 per cent in its Profit After Tax at Rs 145.50 crore for September quarter FY27, on account of elevated input costs and normalisation of the effective tax rate. The company had posted a PAT of Rs 148.35 crore in the July-September period a year ago, according to a regulatory filing from Kolkata-headquartered Emami. Revenue from operations was up 36.2 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,087.65 crore in the September quarter under review. "Input costs remained elevated through the quarter. However, EBITDA grew by 25 per cent to Rs 222 crore and profit before tax grew 29 per cent to Rs 194 crore. Profit after tax was lower largely due to the normalisation of the effective tax rate following the phase-out of fiscal benefits," said Emami in its earnings statement. Total expenses were at Rs 865.33 crore, up 39.57 per cent in the September quarter of FY27. In the quarter, Emami's domestic business grew by 49 per cent

d93d19dc3bb70bb4.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:19 am IST - VISAKHAPATNAM The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board (APPCB) has stepped up measures to curb air and noise pollution across the State, directing district administrations and police, transport and municipal authorities to enforce environmental regulations and monitor pollution levels, particularly during Deepavali. In a recent communication to Collectors, Magistrates, Superintendents of Police, Municipal Commissioners and Police Commissioners of Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam, the Board called for joint inspection teams to prevent the sale, transportation and use of banned firecrackers. It also directed officials to monitor air quality and noise levels in all district headquarters and towns, following orders issued on October 16. The APPCB on Wednesday said its monitoring during Deepavali 2025 had recorded PM10 levels of up to 238 micrograms per cubic metre and PM2.5 levels of 138 micrograms per cubic metre in Visakhapatnam. Only green crackers approved by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI) will be permitted in cities and towns where air quality is moderate or better, subject to court directions. Conventional crackers containing banned chemicals, including barium salts, are prohibited. Permitted packs must carry unique QR codes linked to their registration, licence and test certificates, the Board said. The prescribed noise limits (in dB(A)) are 75 during the day and 70 at night in industrial areas; 65 and 55 in commercial areas; 55 and 45 in residential areas; and 50 and 40 in silence zones. Daytime is from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. and night-time from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Areas within 100 metres of hospitals, educational institutions and courts are designated silence zones, where honking is prohibited. 481be06aae8907b4.title: World Trade Center township on the anvil for Chengalpattu
481be06aae8907b4.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:31 am IST - CHENNAI GTB Developers (GT Bharathi Urban Developers Pvt Ltd) announced that it has been granted a licence by the World Trade Centers Association (WTCA) to develop World Trade Center Chengalpattu. This particular project is planned as an IT integrated township of 100 to 150 acre, rather than an industrial estate. The project has an estimated value of ₹7,000 crore and will be developed in phases over approximately ten years. The proposed masterplan includes commercial and IT office space, hospitality, residences and an education zone. GTB is at an advanced stage of identifying and securing land for the project. GTB is also pursuing a second World Trade Center development in Kanchipuram district, proposed across approximately 500 acres. Unlike Chengalpattu, it is envisaged as an industrial World Trade Center, with manufacturing and data centre zones alongside infrastructure, education and hospitality. GTB intends to explore the project under a public-private partnership (PPP) model, one of the structures under which World Trade Centers are developed globally. Nilakantan Unni, Mahopadhyaya brings to the notice of the public through the columns of the “Malayala Manorama” that there is an interesting image of Buddha in Pallikkal in the Mavelikkara Taluk in central Travancore. It is a stone image exactly similar in appearance to that of the well-known Karumandi Kuttan with which people who have travelled along the backwater route between Alleppey and Quilon, are very familiar. The image is worshipped by the villagers who believe that it is a deity presiding over their destinies. 2c70037c30f39bae.title: Man severely injured after falling from moving train
2c70037c30f39bae.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:25 am IST - Chennai An unidentified person was severely injured after he fell while attempting to board a moving train at Perambur railway station on Wednesday night. The Government Railway Police (GRP) said the 40-year-old man slipped and fell while attempting to board an electric train unit bound for Moore Market Complex station. Factually incorrect: In the 2019 Israeli election (which this appears to reference), Benny Gantz (Blue and White) won the mandate to form a government, not Benny Eisenkot (Yesh Atid). Eisenkot did not win 67 nods to be PM; Gantz's coalition had the majority.

Timeline inconsistency: Herzog typically gives the mandate to the leader of the largest party or a coalition with a majority. Eisenkot's party was not the largest, and no coalition led by him had 61 seats at the time of the initial mandate decision.
Source reliability: The source is a Google News RSS feed, which aggregates headlines from various outlets, leading to a jumbled and potentially contradictory summary.

3722fa8859ea88c9.title: Britannia Q2 net profit rises 10.8% to ₹726 crore on volume growth
3722fa8859ea88c9.summary: Bakery food company Britannia Industries Ltd on Thursday reported an increase of 10.82 per cent rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 725.99 crore for the September quarter of FY27, on a year-on-year basis, led by volume growth. The company had posted a net profit of Rs 655.06 crore in the July-September quarter a year ago, according to a regulatory filing from Britannia Industries. Britannia Industries' revenue from the sale of products was up 16.6 per cent to Rs 5,541.57 crore in the September quarter. The sales growth was "led by volume growth of 13 per cent", said Britannia Industries in its earnings statement. Its revenue from operations was up 15.64 per cent to Rs 5,597.79 crore in the second quarter of FY27. It was at Rs 4,840.63 crore in the corresponding quarter. Britannia's total expenses were at Rs 4,690.47 crore, up 17 per cent in Q2, FY27. Its total income, which includes other income, was up 15.9 per cent to Rs 5,671.30 crore in the September quarter. b9f1a3137bab4876.title: Chawri Bazar building collapse: CM orders inquiry, FIR against contractor
b9f1a3137bab4876.summary: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Thursday ordered an inquiry into the collapse of a three-storey building under construction in Old Delhi's Chawri Bazar, which claimed two lives and left four others injured, and directed the registration of an FIR against the contractor. The chief minister also ordered the immediate suspension of the concerned junior engineer (JE) and assistant engineer (AE) in connection with the incident. She directed officials to ensure the best possible medical treatment for the injured and provide immediate ex-gratia assistance to the affected families. "Stringent action will be taken against those found responsible, in accordance with the law," the chief minister said. The building collapsed around 9.50 am in Gali Sitara, near the Chawri Bazar Metro station, police said. Two bodies were pulled out from the debris by a Delhi Fire Services (DFS) rescue team, while four injured people were taken to a hospital by locals before the fire department teams arrive

93278c0595bfcb2b.title: MSME training programme held at VIT in Vellore
93278c0595bfcb2b.summary: Published - November 05, 2026 12:50 am IST - VELLORE Collector P.S. Leela Alex inaugurates the training programme in the presence of G. Viswanathan, founder and president, VIT, and other dignitaries at VIT campus. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement A month-long smartphone servicing and repair training programme under an entrepreneurship skill development initiative, which was organised by the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector, was held at the campus of Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) in Vellore on Wednesday. Collector P.S. Leela Alex inaugurated the training programme in the presence of G. Viswanathan, founder and president, VIT, Sankar Viswanathan, vice-president, VIT, and Reshma Rajeevan, deputy director, Department of MSME. In his presidential address, Mr. Viswanathan said that the MSME sector forms the backbone of the Indian economy. After agriculture, it is the second-largest employer, providing jobs to around 33 crore people in the country. “Around seven crore MSMEs are registered across the country with Maharashtra leading with one crore MSMEs, followed by Uttar Pradesh with 85 lakh MSMEs. Tamil Nadu comes third with 62 lakh MSMEs. The sector contributes 45 per cent to manufacturing output and 46 per cent to exports,” he said. The Chancellor said that VIT has been implementing a free scholarship scheme - Support The Advancement of Rural Students (STARS) - for government school students. Around ₹103 crore worth of scholarships under the scheme have been distributed to students since the scheme was started, in 2008. VIT has also provided free admissions to 1,200 students between 2008 and 2026 under the scheme. “VIT plans to expand the scheme to the entire country, where beneficiaries will get free education, accommodation, and food. At present, the scheme has been executed only in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh, “ he said. 85edcbb69df72812.title: Cabinet clears ₹14,500 cr funding scheme for battery energy storage systems
85edcbb69df72812.summary: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved Rs 14,500 crore in viability gap funding for 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage systems between FY27 and FY31. This development is significant given India's ambitious target of 500 GW of renewable energy by 2030. The scheme is aimed at supporting the development of 92 GWh storage capacity across three technologies -- Battery Energy Storage System (30 GWh), Pumped Storage Projects (60 GWh) and Emerging Storage Technologies (2GW), Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said in a media briefing here. The minister said the scheme will be implemented for five years till 2030-31.

94436e0dedf1355a.title: Helping hand: On Cyclones Arnab and Murasu
94436e0dedf1355a.summary: Updated - November 05, 2026 01:47 am IST Long-term preparedness and a swift response by authorities minimised casualties when the back-to-back cyclones Arnab and Murasu hit two places of the Andhra Pradesh coast. In Andhra Pradesh, damage from Cyclone Arnab , which made landfall on October 28 was estimated at roughly ₹4,526 crore. Initial estimates of the damage by Cyclone Murasu, which crossed the coast on November 3, indicate that about 52,500 hectares of standing crops were affected. The State reported 12 deaths from the two cyclones. The first cyclone damaged nearly 90,000 hectares of standing crops in southern parts of Odisha. After preliminary on-the-spot assessment of flood-hit areas, the Union government is expected to soon release the first instalment of funds to the affected States. Personnel from Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu have also gone to the rescue of Andhra Pradesh. The deployment of the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) and other technologies has significantly reduced human casualties and property damage. During Cyclone Hudhud in October 2014, Andhra Pradesh reported 63 deaths and damage estimated at nearly ₹22,000 crore. As natural disasters become more frequent in India, greater collaboration is needed between higher learning institutions, especially in science and technology, and central and State government agencies. Authorities must develop an effective compensation framework for saving crops/crop losses. The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, a crop insurance scheme that was launched by the Union government a decade ago, has not provided farmers with comprehensive safety cover, as they suffer due to the vagaries of nature. 94436e0dedf1355a.raw_facts: Updated - November 05, 2026 01:47 am IST Long-term preparedness and a swift response by authorities minimised casualties when the back-to-back cyclones Arnab and Murasu hit two places of the Andhra Pradesh coast. In Andhra Pradesh, damage from Cyclone Arnab , which made landfall on October 28 was estimated at roughly ₹4,526 crore. Initial estimates of the damage by Cyclone Murasu, which crossed the coast on November 3, indicate that about 52,500 hectares of standing crops were affected. The State reported 12 deaths from the two cyclones. The first cyclone damaged nearly 90,000 hectares of standing crops in southern parts of Odisha. After preliminary on-the-spot assessment of flood-hit areas, the Union government is expected to soon release the first instalment of funds to the affected States. Personnel from Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu have also gone to the rescue of Andhra Pradesh. The deployment of the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) and other technologies has significantly reduced human casualties and property damage. During Cyclone Hudhud in October 2014, Andhra Pradesh reported 63 deaths and damage estimated at nearly ₹22,000 crore. As natural disasters become more frequent in India, greater collaboration is needed between higher learning institutions, especially in science and technology, and central and State government agencies. Authorities must develop an effective compensation framework for saving crops/crop losses. The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, a crop insurance scheme that was launched by the Union government a decade ago, has not provided farmers with comprehensive safety cover, as they suffer due to the vagaries of nature. f1be7d22672b238e.title: What the BRICS carbon market partnership needs
f1be7d22672b238e.summary: Updated - November 05, 2026 12:34 am IST ‘A common framework for measurement, reporting and verification should be the partnership’s first deliverable’ | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto On September 12, at the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, the New Delhi Declaration confirmed that BRICS members look forward to implementing the Memorandum of Understanding on the BRICS Carbon Markets Partnership. The commitment remains modest: on capacity-building and experience-sharing, with no trading framework, targets or timeline. The Rio summit acknowledged the memorandum in 2025, and New Delhi has reiterated it. With India’s BRICS presidency entering its final quarter, operationalising the partnership requires not so much a common trading platform as a common rulebook. Eight BRICS members reportedly operate voluntary markets, and Brazil, China, India and Indonesia host over a third of the carbon credit projects registered worldwide. Compliance systems are maturing, too. China’s emissions trading system (ETS) — added steel, cement and aluminium through its 2024-25 allocation plan. India’s Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) has notified emission-intensity targets for 490 entities across nine sectors and opened an offset mechanism. Brazil’s Law of 2024 establishes the Brazilian Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading System (SBCE), a cap-and-trade system. However, none of these markets is linked to another. 267e6e0b1edf3f44.title: SC upholds states' power to levy additional tax on sales tax under pre-GST regime
267e6e0b1edf3f44.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday reaffirmed states’ power to impose an additional tax, surcharge or cess calculated on an existing sales tax, settling a legal question that had remained unresolved for nearly three decades. A seven-judge Constitution Bench upheld a 1974 judgment that recognized such levies as an exercise of states’ taxation powers under the pre-GST regime. A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant held that an additional levy calculated as a percentage of the sales tax payable by a dealer amounts to an increase in the sales-tax rate. It therefore falls within Entry 54 of the State List, which empowered states to tax the sale or purchase of goods, other than inter-state sales, before the introduction of the goods and services tax (GST) in 2017. The ruling reaffirms the Supreme Court’s 1974 decision in S. Kodar vs State of Kerala , which upheld an additional sales tax imposed by Tamil Nadu on dealers whose annual turnover exceeded specified limits. The court had held that the levy, calculated as a percentage of sales tax payable, was an increase in the sales-tax rate rather than a tax on dealers’ income. Entry 54 provided the constitutional basis for states’ sales-tax powers before GST . Following the introduction of GST, states have retained the power to tax certain products outside its ambit, including petrol, diesel, crude oil , natural gas, aviation turbine fuel and alcoholic liquor for human consumption. In a concurring judgment, Justice K.V. Viswanathan said Kodar was correctly decided and remained good law, requiring no reconsideration. The bench also held that there was no conflict between Kodar and the Supreme Court’s 1983 judgment in Hoechst Pharmaceuticals, which had upheld a similar surcharge on sales tax. The court observed that the broader reference had become academic following the introduction of GST in 2017 and subsequent changes to the constitutional provisions and state taxation laws. 5b4e0ad92f8d80c5.summary: Updated - November 05, 2026 02:46 am IST - HYDERABAD Orange alert was sounded for Bhadradri Kothagudem district for Wednesday (November 4, 2026), and yellow for Khammam and Mulugu in Telangana | Photo Credit: India Meteorological Department A mandal each in Khammam and Bhadradri Kothagudem in Telangana, which were under red alert due to the impact of cyclone Murasu on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), received extremely heavy rainfall between 204 mm and 235 mm on the intervening night of Tuesday and Wednesday (November 3 and 4, 2026). And, some more mandals in the two districts received very heavy rainfall between 150 mm and 204 mm. Of the two, Bhadradri Kothagudem did not get a break from the extremely heavy rain on Wednesday as a mandal there received 278.5 mm, as per Telangana Development Planning Society’s rainfall data till 8.00 p.m. The highest of 278.5 mm in Aswaraopet was followed by 188.3 mm in Malkaram in Dammapeta mandal, 175 mm in Ankampalem in Dammapeta and 149.8 mm in Mulakalapally. India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centres in its impact weather bulletin issued at 11 a.m. has placed Bhadradri Kothagudem under orange alert indicating heavy to very heavy rain on Wednesday. Moderate to heavy rain was predicted in Mulugu and Khammam. The highest amount of rainfall in Khammam was 13.5 mm in JVR OCP I&II, 6.3 mm in Pedapalli and 4.5 mm in Mancherial. The highest of 235 mm in Mulakapalle of Bhadradri Kothagudem was followed by 204.7 mm in Vemsoor of Khammam, as per Telangana Development Planning Society’s latest weather report issued in the morning on Wednesday (November 4, 2026). 46c2bf304f6451ed.title: Iran exempts Indian ships from Hormuz curbs, citing medicine imports
46c2bf304f6451ed.summary: Iran has exempted commercial ships from four countries, including India and China, from transit restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz, a top Iranian official has said, amid continued attacks on vessels attempting to cross the strategic waterway. Amir Hayat Moghadam, Deputy Chairman of the Iranian Parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, made the announcement in an interview with the Iranian Students' News Agency (ISNA) on Tuesday. "We have currently exempted four countries - India, China, Iraq and Qatar - from transit restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz. Ships from these countries pass freely, and the Americans do not intercept them either," he was quoted as saying by the semi-official news agency. Moqaddam said the exemptions were based on specific considerations and mutual interests. He said that facilitating the passage of Indian ships was intended to allow imports of medicines from India, while the exemption for Chinese vessels was intended to secure Beijing

4f0905bdfb61cff0.title: Class 3 student dies after collapsing in classroom, police register case
4f0905bdfb61cff0.summary: Published - November 05, 2026 04:30 am IST A nine-year-old Class 3 student died after collapsing inside her classroom at a school in Mayur Vihar, east Delhi, on Wednesday morning. The police have registered a case under Section 194 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita in connection with the death and examined the CCTV footage to ascertain the circumstances leading to the incident. The incident occurred around 9.20 a.m., when the girl returned to her classroom after a sports period and collapsed while standing in front of her class teacher, Deputy Commissioner of Police (East District) Rajeev Kumar said. According to the police, a Police Control Room (PCR) call reporting the incident was received around 9.52 a.m. The school authorities rushed her to Vimla Devi Hospital and subsequently shifted her to Malik Radix Health Care in Nirman Vihar, where she was declared brought dead. The CCTV footage showed the girl attempting to approach her class teacher before suddenly collapsing. The teacher immediately rushed to her aid and tried to make her sit on a chair, while other students gathered around her. Some of her classmates rushed out to alert the school authorities. The victim’s family alleged that she was not given timely medical attention or CPR. The police, however, clarified that CCTV footage showed the teacher attending to her immediately. School principal Dr. Bhavna said the hospital informed the school authorities that the girl had suffered a cardiac arrest. She added that the school staff had also informed the girl’s family members. a98e4d254a85d381.title: Mobile orthopaedic and spine care unit launched
a98e4d254a85d381.summary: Updated - November 05, 2026 12:48 am IST It will facilitate the early assessment of conditions such as arthritis, osteoporosis, fractures, and spinal disorders. Kauvery Hospital Vadapalani, in collaboration with Hexaware Technologies, launched a Mobile Orthopaedic and Spine Care Unit, as part of a Corporate Social Responsibility initiative to extend specialised orthopaedic and spine care to rural and remote communities. The unit is equipped with a digital X-ray system, which is provided with an onboard reader and Bone Mineral Density (BMD) assessment facilities. The initiative places special emphasis on senior citizens, people with mobility limitations, as well as those facing challenges in travelling to hospitals for medical consultations and investigations. It will facilitate the early assessment of conditions such as arthritis, osteoporosis, fractures, and spinal disorders. Digital X-rays will help doctors evaluate bone and joint conditions, fractures, and spinal abnormalities, while BMD assessments will help identify individuals who are at risk of low bone density and osteoporosis, according to a press release. 6afd482cd8ed8670.title: Celebrations among NDA alliance leaders after landslide victory
6afd482cd8ed8670.summary: Published - November 05, 2026 01:22 am IST - VIJAYAWADA Celebrations broke out among NDA alliance leaders and workers in Vijayawada following the alliance’s emphatic victory in the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation elections. MP Kesineni Sivanath, East MLA Gadde Ramamohan, NTR district parliamentary constituency in-charge M. Mallikarjuna Rao, BJP NTR district president Gadde Anuradha and others participated in the programme. They felicitated the newly-elected Mayor Vangaveeti Radha Krishna on Wednesday. Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Sivanath pointed out that people have demonstrated their confidence in the NDA alliance through the election results. Despite the relatively low voter turnout, people had given the alliance such a decisive mandate, he said. The MP said the victory had placed greater responsibility on the alliance and assured that they would live up to people’s expectations by developing Vijayawada in all sectors. The MP said the delay in finalising seat-sharing arrangements within the alliance and certain other factors had cost them victory in another three to four divisions. He said they were always willing to consider constructive suggestions from anyone, including former IPS officer A.B. Venkateswara Rao, if they were beneficial to the people and the party. Later, Mr. Radha Krishna expressed his gratitude to Jana Sena Party president and Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan for giving him the opportunity to serve as Mayor and to Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu for encouraging him. He also thanked the people of Vijayawada for their confidence in him. They expressed confidence that the city would be transformed into a developed urban centre by prioritising infrastructure, sanitation, drinking water supply, roads and the resolution of public grievances, in line with the hopes and aspirations of Vijayawada residents. efc24c56c9547236.raw_facts: Implementation of Section 51A of UAPA, 1967: Updates to UNSC’s 1988(2011) Sanctions List: Amendment of 05 Entries SEBI
flags: UAPA was enacted in 1967, but Section 51A does not exist in the original 1967 act; the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act was amended in 2019, and Section 51A is not a standard section number associated with UAPA implementation in this context.
UNSC Resolution 1988 was adopted in 2011, but the phrasing '1988(2011)' is non-standard; typically, resolutions are cited by year and number (e.g., Res. 1988 (2011)).
SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) does not implement UAPA or manage UN sanctions lists; this is the responsibility of the Ministry of Home Affairs and the UN Security Council.
The title conflates unrelated legal and regulatory bodies (UAPA, UNSC, SEBI) in a way that is factually incoherent.

f5694e718054dbc5.title: Police ARSI suspended for allegedly reporting for duty drunk, misbehaving with public
f5694e718054dbc5.summary: Published - November 05, 2026 12:57 am IST - Bengaluru The public also demanded that the officer undergo an alcohol breathalyser test to establish whether he was drunk while on duty. | Image for representational purposes only | Photo Credit: File photo An Assistant Reserve Sub-Inspector (ARSI) attached to the CAR Western Squad has been placed under immediate suspension following allegations of misconduct while allegedly under the influence of alcohol during bandobast duty within the limits of Annapoorneshwari Nagar Police Station. The suspended officer has been identified as Gopal B. Rathod. According to sources, members of the public objected to his behaviour after noticing that he was allegedly intoxicated. A heated argument ensued, which escalated when some people allegedly roughed him up before handing him over to Hoysala patrolling police personnel. The public also demanded that the officer undergo an alcohol breathalyser test to establish whether he was drunk while on duty. One of the people present recorded the incident on a mobile phone and circulated the video on social media, tagging the Home Minister and the Bengaluru City Police Commissioner and demanding action against the officer. The video and the incident reportedly caused embarrassment among senior police officials, who directed the jurisdictional Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) to conduct an inquiry and initiate strict action. Following the incident, Gopal B. Rathod was placed under immediate suspension pending a departmental inquiry. 4395ff41a3d444f2.title: Police Inspector awarded two-month imprisonment in contempt case
4395ff41a3d444f2.summary: Published - November 05, 2026 12:58 am IST - HYDERABAD The Telangana High Court awarded two-month imprisonment to a police officer of the rank of Inspector, holding him guilty in a contempt of court case. Justice C.V. Bhaskar Reddy of the HC also imposed a fine of ₹ 2,000 on Inspector M. Prem Kumar. The sentence, however, was suspended for two weeks providing an opportunity to the Inspector for an appeal. The contempt case was filed by A. Sekhar Babu and seven others contending that the Inspector failed to provide aid to protect their plots despite specific orders from the HC - passed in 2023. The petitioners, majority of them senior citizens, stated that despite a specific direction from a single judge of the HC to provide protection to them from illegal interference by three persons (who were made respondents in the writ petition), the then Station House Officer Prem Kumar failed to act. The Inspector contended that he had no knowledge of the earlier order of the HC in the matter. “However, the absence of prior knowledge of the an order cannot justify inaction. It was incumbent upon him to examine the order and take appropriate steps in accordance with law to ensure its implementation,” the judge noted. f86538e708eec70e.title: Police seize 72 kg of ganja, gutka in Vellore, Tirupattur
f86538e708eec70e.summary: Published - November 05, 2026 12:54 am IST - VELLORE Searches, using sniffer dogs, were held at public places such as railway station on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement In a special drive, the District Police in Vellore and Tirupattur have seized 72 kilograms of ganja and gukta in various public places and arrested six drug peddlers on Wednesday. The police identified the arrested persons as Rajesh Kumar, 32, Ali Khan, 52, Suresh, 37, Akbar, 53, Harish, 35, and Balaraman, 65. They belonged to Vellore and Tirupattur. Based on orders of Superintendent of Police N.U. Sivaraman and Akshay Anil Wakhare of Vellore and Tirupattur districts respectively, special teams were formed to conduct surprise checks at public places in these districts. The police said sniffer dogs were also roped in during searches at railway stations, bus termini, and other public places during the day-long drive. The teams seized 35 kg of ganja and 37 kg of gukta in these two districts. The police said most of the contraband were sourced from agents in Andhra Pradesh, for sale in industrial regions such as Ranipet, Sriperambadur, Vaniyambadi, Ambur, Vellore and Cheyyar. Cases were registered and arrested persons were lodged in prison. A probe is under way. db9af969a6cac92d.title: Two 17-year-old students sexually assaulted at party, two booked under PoCSO
db9af969a6cac92d.summary: Published - November 05, 2026 01:02 am IST - HYDERABAD Two 17-year-old girl students were allegedly sexually assaulted after being made to consume alcohol at a party in Balanagar on the night of October 1. Police have registered a case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act against two youths in connection with the incident. The suspects have been identified as Ganesh alias Ghana, 19, and Tarun, 26, who is married. Ganesh was in a relationship with one of the victims and had invited her to the party. She took a friend along with her. According to Madhura Nagar police Inspector H. Prabhakar, after taking the two students to the venue, the youths allegedly made them consume alcohol before sexually assaulting them. “The students had consumed one beer each. One of the victims later fell unwell and was taken to a hospital, where suspicion arose of a possible sexual assault,” said the officer, adding that when questioned, the students disclosed what had happened. Their statements were subsequently recorded at a Bharosa Centre. The students were admitted to a hospital in Madhuranagar following the incident. They later approached the Madhuranagar police and lodged a complaint, based on which a case was registered and an investigation taken up. The case will be transferred to Balanagar police on jurisdictional grounds. 6660dd9e7606f22f.title: RBI starts 3 surveys to capture inflation expectations, consumer confidence
6660dd9e7606f22f.summary: Reserve Bank on Tuesday announced three key surveys to capture inflation expectations of households and gauge consumer confidence in the country- the studies that provide input for bi-monthly monetary policy. The central bank has announced the launch of the November 2026 round of the Inflation Expectations Survey of Households (IESH). "The November 2026 round of the survey is being launched. The survey aims at capturing subjective assessments on price movements and inflation, based on their individual consumption baskets," it said. The study will be conducted across 19 cities -- Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Chennai, Delhi, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Jammu, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Patna, Raipur, Ranchi and Thiruvananthapuram. In another statement, the RBI said the Urban Consumer Confidence Survey seeks qualitative responses from households regarding their sentiments on the general economic situation, employment scenario, price level, households'

Velu for the party’s Northern Zone Youth Wing Conference held on December 14, 2025. DVAC sources said that the drone survey was conducted in coordination with the Revenue Department, Tiruvannamalai Corporation, and the police to assess the extent of damage done to the water body. It will also provide total depth and width of the tank that was mined for the purpose. by illegal sand mining. The assessment comes in the wake of a complaint filed by Arappor Iyakkam , an NGO, with the DVAC at its headquarters in Chennai on August 13 this year. The complaint alleged that large volumes of sand was illegally mined from the irrigation tank reportedly based on directions by the then PWD and Highways Minister Mr. Velu. The sand theft has reportedly incurred a loss to a tune of ₹8 crore to State exchequer, the complainant claimed. cb6a087f49e6adf0.title: RBI eases forex rules for services exports and imports
cb6a087f49e6adf0.summary: The changes form part of the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) which came into effect from October 1, 2026. Under the amended regulations, a resident individual exporting services will be deemed to have submitted the Export Declaration Form, or EDF, once the individual provides the authorised dealer bank with the information required to credit the payment to the exporter's account. No transaction-value threshold has been prescribed for resident individuals.

b076dd70c49e380d.title: In Tehran, a search for the future of West Asian security
b076dd70c49e380d.summary: Updated - November 04, 2026 01:26 am IST ‘Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan travelling to Iran for this exchange came as a surprise to many given that Tehran had struck several Arab countries in response to American and Israeli aggression’ | Photo Credit: AP More than eight months after the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran , West Asia remains on tenterhooks, as the United States, Israel, and Iran continue to flirt with a resumption of military hostilities. Elections in Israel as well as the U.S. midterm polls offered an interesting pause, even as war rhetoric remained high. Amid these tensions, an alliance of Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan, known as the “Mecca Agreement”, arrived in Iran’s capital in October to discuss regional security. A large part of Iran’s response since the U.S. and Israel began bombing the country in February 2026 has been to target American interests, including data centres, and military installations across the Gulf states. This forms part of Tehran’s strategy of asymmetric warfare, shaped by its view of the conflict as an existential threat to the Islamic Republic, particularly following the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in an airstrike. 0341b26a696066b0.title: On the Arunachal frontier, silence is not a strategy
0341b26a696066b0.summary: Updated - November 04, 2026 01:18 am IST ‘Candour will strengthen New Delhi’s hand in dealing with Beijing’ | Photo Credit: THE HINDU/RITU RAJ KONWAR For some time, reports have circulated of transgressions by China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA) in the Asaphila, Taksing and Longju areas of Arunachal Pradesh. The facts are neither clear nor officially acknowledged. Yet, there are signals that something out of the ordinary is happening along this stretch of the border. The matter warrants close attention. The clearest signal came on October 22, 2026. Speaking at an Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) function, Director General Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor said: “In the past few days, a situation arose where face-off happened at several locations in Arunachal and it still continues.” This was the first official confirmation of the scale of the problem. This daily reported, citing “government sources”, that the two sides had been in a stand-off at Asaphila, near Taksing, since late July. Direct plans have lower expense ratios compared to regular plans, benefiting long-term investors through compounded returns. These changes aim to reduce conflicts of interest associated with higher commission payments in regular plans.

fd0d1593764da810.title: Coming of age: On the Binance hack
fd0d1593764da810.summary: Updated - November 04, 2026 12:58 am IST The recent hack at Binance, the biggest theft ever at the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lessons for India. But Indian policymakers must be careful to learn the right ones. First, it must be understood that the hack is not an indictment of the crypto space itself . Being a crypto exchange did not make Binance more vulnerable than if it were, say, a bank. Hacking is now a daily occurrence across sectors and even small pharmaceutical companies often have to fend off millions of attacks a month. Of course, Binance must look into how it was hacked and prevent a recurrence, but the cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security software developers is a perpetual one. For every million, or even billion, attacks that are stopped, one will inevitably get through. The lesson for Indian policymakers is not that crypto is unsafe in itself; this incident does not prove that. Rather, it is about how Binance prepared for and reacted to the attack. Back in 2018, Binance had set up an emergency fund called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets in the event of a security breach or platform-level incident. The fund was created for exactly this kind of incident, and was financed through trading fees that Binance collects from users. Since the $6.3 billion worth of assets stolen exceeded the SAFU’s resources, Binance dipped into its own resources to restore about 95% of users’ assets within four days of the hack. So, Binance used a stable source of revenue to finance an emergency fund, which it deployed when an emergency occurred. The system worked perfectly, also showing how maturely and responsibly the crypto space can be run. The Indian government and the Reserve Bank of India still view the private crypto space as the Wild West of techno-finance. This is no longer the case. Large crypto companies are employing prudential practices, safeguarding customers, and cooperating with law enforcement agencies. I

ea8eeda99dc14955.summary: Updated - November 04, 2026 12:54 am IST Months after a sham election that installed junta chief Min Aung Hlaing as Myanmar’s civilian President, the military continues to wage war on its own people even as the world has largely looked away. More than a lakh people are estimated to have died since the 2021 coup, many in fighting between the junta and the anti-coup People’s Defence Forces and ethnic armed organisations. The junta has also killed thousands of civilians in air strikes on villages in rebel-held areas to terrorise communities into giving up their resistance. With wars affecting Ukraine, Gaza, Sudan and Yemen, and Iran, the world has grown numb to such violence. The junta has exploited that indifference and a shifting geopolitical situation to act with impunity. Russia and China, its principal arms suppliers, have stood by it with the former supplying jets that were used to bomb civilians. Beijing, which tacitly allowed three ethnic armed organisations to launch an offensive in Shan and Rakhine States in late 2023, has since pressured two of them into ceasefires and returning seized territory. It also backed the January election. Since being sworn in, Min Aung Hlaing has visited India , Thailand, Vietnam and three other ASEAN member-states. ASEAN still swears by its Five-Point Consensus, which calls for an end to violence and dialogue. Yet, its members seem more than eager to do business with a regime that has flouted every point. Meanwhile, U.S. officials reportedly held secret talks with the junta in Tokyo in June and October, and a senior delegation met Min Aung Hlaing in Naypyidaw in September. Japan is reportedly pressing the Financial Action Task Force to take Myanmar off its blacklist. The motives are not hard to understand. China wants an outlet to the Indian Ocean and security for its oil and gas pipelines. District teams have also begun physically verifying the proposed premises. The North District received around 25 applications as of Tuesday evening. Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) Niharika Bhatt said verification had begun and licences were expected to be issued from Tuesday night. “The Central District has six permanent licence holders and has not received any applications for temporary licences so far. It received three applications for temporary licences in 2025,” said DCP Rohit Rajbir Singh. The police, along with Delhi Fire Services officials, are inspecting the proposed premises, verifying applicants’ credentials and checking ownership or tenancy documents. The checks also cover applicants’ criminal antecedents and compliance with prescribed safety conditions. Officials said the verification process usually takes a few hours. Fire Chief A.K. Malik said Fire Department officials would assess whether the premises were accessible to firefighting vehicles and complied with fire safety requirements. “Temporary sheds must be made of non-flammable material, with at least three metres between sheds and 50 metres from protected works (such as residential buildings, educational institutions, hospitals, places of worship, markets and other public spaces). c01f2a67a822c282.title: Rajanna is free to quit party if he wishes: Balakrishna
c01f2a67a822c282.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 12:43 am IST - Bengaluru H.C. Balakrishna. | Photo Credit: File photo Congress leader and Minister for Municipal Administration H.C. Balakrishna lashed out at senior Congress leader and MLA K.N. Rajanna on Tuesday, saying he was free to quit the party if he so wished, and accusing him of “betraying the party while being part of it.” This comes against the backdrop of Mr. Rajanna’s son and MLC R. Rajendra recently meeting JD(S) leader and Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy. Speaking to reporters in Chitradurga, he said, “If Mr. Rajanna wants to leave the party and join another party, he is free to do so. Let him honestly answer whether his son contested the election fairly. The election process had not even concluded when he posed for a photograph with Mr. Kumaraswamy. If the Congress party does not pay attention to such issues, it may have to face serious problems in the future. Mr. Rajanna is betraying the party while remaining in it. The party does not belong to any one individual. He has engaged in anti-party activities, and strict action should be taken against him. We will lodge a complaint against Mr. Rajanna with the party high command.” Published - November 04, 2026 12:43 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 3d972eaddd00d5f1.title: Man undergoing de-addiction treatment dies at private clinic in Kodungaiyur
3d972eaddd00d5f1.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 12:36 am IST - CHENNAI A 28-year-old man undergoing treatment for alcohol addiction at a private clinic in Kodungaiyur died on Monday. His family members alleged that medical negligence at the clinic led to his death. A senior police officer said, “We have registered a case of unnatural death. Further action will be taken only after receiving the post-mortem and viscera examination reports.” The deceased was identified as Lokesh, 28, Lokesh was assisting his father in real estate business. He had recently developed an addiction to alcohol. His family admitted him to a private de-addiction clinic in Moolakadai last week within the jurisidiction of Kodungaiyur police. A staff member at the clinic administered him an injection after his health condition deteriorated. As his condition worsened, his family members rushed him to another private hospital in Madhavaram, where doctors declared him brought dead. His body was subsequently brought back to the clinic in Moolakadai. Following this, his relatives and family members staged a protest outside the clinic, accusing its staff of negligence. Police personnel intervened and pacified them after receiving a complaint. The body was sent to Government Stanley Hospital for post-mortem examination. 2c927a6756e4bfd8.summary: Zydus Wellness on Tuesday reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 5.1 crore in the September quarter due to higher revenues. The company posted a net loss of Rs 52.8 crore in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year, the company said in a regulatory filing. Its revenue from operations rose sharply to Rs 1,126.6 crore in the quarter under review, up from Rs 650.5 crore in the year-ago period, it added. Total expenses increased to Rs 1,125.4 crore in the July-September period from Rs 668.3 crore a year earlier. Zydus Wellness shares were trading 0.63 per cent higher at Rs 486.25 apiece on the BSE.

7c17651bbd4e339c.title: Pfizer Q2 results: Net profit rises 65.7% to ₹313 cr, income at ₹774 cr
7c17651bbd4e339c.summary: Drugmaker Pfizer Ltd on Tuesday reported a 65.72 per cent increase in net profit to Rs 313.25 crore in the September quarter, driven by gains from exceptional items. The company had posted a profit of Rs 189 crore in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year, Pfizer said in a regulatory filing. Pfizer has accounted for exceptional gains of Rs 132.06 crore in the September quarter from its parent entity Pfizer Inc USA following the sale of Minipress XL. Consequent to the decision, Pfizer Ltd discontinued the manufacture of Minipress XL from September 7, 2026, according to the filing. Its profit before tax and exceptional items stood at Rs 290.77 crore during the quarter under review, up 13.86 per cent year-on-year. It was at Rs 255.37 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year. Its total income rose to Rs 774.19 crore during the quarter under review from Rs 684.19 crore in the year-ago period. Pfizer reported an increase in total expenses to Rs 483.2

d05f7360afb4ab22.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 01:51 am IST - KANNUR A mobile phone and accessories, including two power banks, a charger and three data cables, were seized from Kannur Central Jail during a search by prison officials on Monday. The prohibited articles were found hidden beneath stone slabs behind the jail’s second block. The Town police have registered a case and launched an investigation based on a complaint lodged by jail Joint Superintendent A. Shaiju. The repeated seizure of prohibited articles from within the jail compound has raised concerns over security checks. Inadequate inspection of food items and cooking materials brought into the prison is suspected to be facilitating the smuggling of such articles. e971873e9869d8c6.title: Bengaluru: South corporation shuts 63 commercial establishments in residential layouts
e971873e9869d8c6.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 12:42 am IST - Bengaluru The Corporation sealed the highest number of establishments in the BTM Layout Assembly constituency, where 30 shops were shut. | Photo Credit: Image for representational purpose The Bengaluru South City Corporation has sealed 63 commercial establishments operating “illegally” in residential areas across its jurisdiction during a special enforcement drive conducted by officials. The Corporation sealed the highest number of establishments in the BTM Layout Assembly constituency, where 30 shops were shut. This was followed by 10 in the Bengaluru South constituency, nine in Bommanahalli, eight in Padmanabhanagar, four in Jayanagar, and two within the limits of the Anekal Assembly constituency (part of which falls under the South City Corporation). According to Corporation officials, the action targeted commercial establishments operating in residential areas in violation of regulations. Officials said they were causing inconvenience to residents and obstructing vehicular movement. Bakeries, eateries, condiment stores, salons, beauty parlours, fruit and vegetable outlets, hardware stores, and other commercial establishments were among those sealed. 2fec4d1b944ad2de.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 05:30 am IST - Chennai SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST) will open applications for SRM Joint Entrance Examination (SRMJEE) for all courses on November 4. Applications will be available from 2 p.m. on the website www.srmist.edu.in for Engineering and Technology, Architecture, Management, Liberal Arts and Business Studies, Law, Medicine and Health Sciences, Hotel Management, and Agricultural Sciences programmes. The SRMJEE for undergraduate and postgraduate courses in engineering will be held in over 160 centres across the country. The first phase for the B.Tech, M.Tech, and M.Tech (integrated) engineering programmes will be held on April 17 and 18, 2027, and the last date to apply is April 2, 2027. The second phase will be held on June 19 and 20, 2027, and the last date to apply is June 4, 2027. SRM Law Entrance Test will be held between January 5, 2027 and June 30, 2027 through on-demand centre-based tests. The last date for applying is June 25, 2027. Students appearing for SRMJEE for Management can take the test online between January 11, 2027 and June 30, 2027 for which the last date for applying is June 25, 2027. Similarly, students appearing for SRMJEE for undergraduate and postgraduate courses in Health Sciences can take the test online in two phases. The first phase will be held on April 9 and 10, 2027, and the last date for application is April 4, 2027. The second phase will be held on June 11 and 12, 2027, and the last date to apply is June 6, 2027. For post-PG programmes, the exam will be held on April 9 and 10, 2027, and the last date for applying is April 4, 2027. SRMJEE toppers will receive Founder’s Scholarship that entails a 100% waiver of tuition and hostel fees. Besides, students will also be offered merit scholarships of 25% to 100% tuition fee waivers based on ranks across phases, subjects, and campus-specific criteria, according to a press release. c3ef18c2e0ed82e2.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 01:10 am IST - Bengaluru A candidate in Haveri, who was flagged for poor academic record and emerging as a topper in VAO exam, has now been found to have used a mobile phone during the exam. | Photo Credit: K. MURALI KUMAR Taking into account the irregularities reported at the Shiggaon examination centre of Haveri district in the Village Administrative Officer (VAO) recruitment examination recently, the Karnataka Examination Authority (KEA) has decided to introduce several additional security measures. A candidate in Haveri, who was flagged for poor academic record and emerging as a topper in VAO exam, has now been found to have used a mobile phone during the exam. Haveri police are probing the case now. To prevent such instances, from now on, two invigilators will be appointed for every examination hall. One invigilator will stand at the rear of the hall to monitor candidates, while the other will remain at the front. They will also be responsible for ensuring that the mobile signal jammer in the examination centre is functioning properly. Although candidates are required to undergo thorough frisking before entering the examination centre, it was found that this rule had not been implemented seriously. Therefore, KEA has decided to conduct a second round of checking inside the examination hall as well. All candidates must reach the examination centre at least 30 minutes before the examination begins. Candidates arriving at the last minute will not be permitted to enter, H. Prasanna, Executive Director, KEA said. “Instructions have already been issued to establish district-level monitoring systems to oversee examination centres through webcasting. Going forward, KEA has also decided to appoint a separate invigilator at each examination centre to monitor CCTV footage,” he added. f678e794988cf1e5.title: Security guard dies in fire at Peravallur warehouse
f678e794988cf1e5.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 12:38 am IST - CHENNAI A 54-year-old security guard died of suffocation after a fire broke out at an e-commerce warehouse on SRP Koil Road in Peravallur on Tuesday morning. The warehouse, located on the first floor of a building, had been rented by an online delivery company to store goods ordered by customers. It had been functioning for the past two years. The fire broke out around 6.30 a.m. when the warehouse was closed. Ramamoorthy, 54, a security guard on duty, noticed thick smoke billowing out and entered the premises to locate the source of the fire. However, the blaze spread rapidly, trapping him inside. He collapsed due to suffocation. Fire and Rescue Services personnel from Kolathur and Sembium rushed to the spot and put out the fire. They rescued Ramamoorthy and took him to Periyar Nagar Government Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Peravallur police have registered a case and are investigating the cause of the fire. An electrical short circuit is suspected to have triggered the blaze. According to a press release, Darez Ahamed, Secretary, Tamil Nadu Department of Health and Family Welfare Department, was the chief guest. In his address, Mr. Ahamed highlighted CMC’s long-standing commitment to serving underserved communities. He also emphasised challenges faced by graduates, including an ageing population, the rise in non-communicable diseases, antimicrobial resistance, and climate change related health challenges. The official also highlighted the growing role of artificial intelligence in healthcare. A total of 189 postgraduates were presented certificates by the college principal, Solomon Sathishkumar, in the presence of Vaibhav Londhe, Associate Director, CMC, and I. ff01b48fc3db8bdb.title: RPF head constable saves passenger from being dragged by train at Perambur railway station
ff01b48fc3db8bdb.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 12:33 am IST - CHENNAI A Railway Protection Force (RPF) head constable saved a 23-year-old passenger from being dragged along by a moving train at the Perambur railway station on Tuesday. The incident occurred when Train No. 12672 Nilgiri Superfast Express was departing from Platform 1. Mohammed Kajim Alam, who realised that he had boarded the wrong train, attempted to alight while it was moving. He lost his balance, clung to the grab rails near the coach doorway, and was dragged on the platform. Noticing the danger, RPF head constable Bhagchand Meena came to his rescue and pulled him away from the moving train, averting a possible tragedy. The passenger’s brother subsequently pulled the alarm chain, bringing the train to a halt. The dates of the visit are yet to be announced officially. Foreign Secretary Misri is paying an official visit to Nepal from November 4-5 at the invitation of Nepal's Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai, the Foreign Ministry here said in a statement.
