e1174ed557d93b84.title: 7,000 kg of unhygienic, foul-smelling khoya seized, destroyed: Delhi CMO
e1174ed557d93b84.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 03:49 am IST - New Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the government would not compromise on public health. File photo: X/@gupta_rekha via ANI. The Food Safety Department of the Delhi government carried out an inspection at Mori Gate Khoya Market on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) and seized and destroyed about 7,000 kg of unhygienic and foul-smelling khoya, taking the total quantity of khoya destroyed by the department so far to 10,660 kg, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the government would not compromise on public health, and ensuring that people have access to safe and quality food during the festive season is one of the government’s foremost responsibilities. “Those involved in food adulteration, regardless of how influential they may be, will be brought within the ambit of the law and face strict action,” she said. Also, 35 of 44 samples of khoya failed preliminary tests at the ‘Food Safety on Wheels’ mobile testing facility. Two additional samples were also collected and sent to a laboratory for detailed examination. “The preliminary tests conducted at the site also brought to light information relating to milk powder, vanaspati and substances used for binding in the suspected material. Samples have been sent to the laboratory for further investigation into these ingredients,” an official statement said. The Food Safety Department has been conducting sustained drives against food adulteration in view of the festive season. As part of the action taken so far, the department destroyed 2,830 kg of khoya on September 4, 610 kg on September 8 and 520 kg on October 23, as per the CMO. flags: Anachronism: The 2024 US midterm elections occurred in November 2024, but Donald Trump was not the incumbent president facing a 'verdict' in that election; he was a former president and the Republican nominee for the 2024 presidential election (which took place in November 2024, not midterms). Midterms are held in even years not divisible by 4 (e.g., 2022, 2026).

Factual Error: The 2022 midterm elections were seen as a verdict on President Biden, not Trump. The 2018 midterms were a verdict on Trump, but the context of 'Iran war' and 'rising fuel costs' does not align with the primary narratives of 2018 (which focused on healthcare, trade, and Trump's first term).

Contextual Mismatch: There was no active 'Iran war' during the 2022 or 2018 US midterm election cycles. While tensions existed, a full-scale war was not a defining feature of those specific midterm contests.

Source Mismatch: Business Standard is an Indian news outlet. While they cover US news, the phrasing and specific combination of issues suggest a potential fabrication or a misdated/misattributed article.

74e5df1dfed40c77.title: Kasi, food for soul
74e5df1dfed40c77.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 04:49 am IST Kasi is often called Anna Kshetra since Goddess Annapoorani, an incarnation of Parvati, resides there permanently. Coming down to earth to undertake a penance for a playful sport with Siva leading to consequences, She chose Kasi at a time when the town was reeling under severe famine. Armed with a ladle and a pot, She brought back prosperity and stayed on, heeding the local king’s request, and continued to bless devotees, said P. Swaminathan. The sacred town attracted saints, sages and ordinary devotees as well, especially around Deepavali. Long ago, Narayana Dikshitar, a staunch devotee who resided there, often invited holy men to his home and fed them humbly. On one occasion, after inviting a group of sadhus for a meal, he reached home only to find his wife bedridden. The guests were due in a couple of hours and a harassed Dikshitar went out seeking a solution. Just outside his house he spotted a woman walking past. Richly adorned, she had a talisman around her neck and a diamond nose ring. She looked at him kindly and the man blurted out his predicament. With a smile, she offered to help prepare the meal for the sadhus. The meal was a stupendous success and all the holy men blessed him. The woman had left the place after her duties and only then did Dikshitar realise that he had not even offered a meal to the woman who came to his aid. He went to bed with that thought and had a dream wherein he apologised to her and asked to see her; the woman declared that she was Annapoorani. She affirmed that She would always remain with those who have a good heart and a supplicatory mind. Informing him that She had left a green turban on the eastern wall of the house, She instructed Dikshitar to install her idol there. “I will remain here forever,” said Annapoorani. Visiting Kasi around Deepavali is considered highly efficacious. Published - November 04, 2026 04:49 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to

1bceed40d8213fab.summary: Citing a World Bank report, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday said around 50 crore people had been lifted out of extreme poverty in India over the last 10 to 12 years, noting that the fight against poverty was limited to "slogans" in the past. Modi doubled down on the development agenda; underlined "transformation" in urban transport infrastructure over the past 12 years, and maintained that empowering the poor and delivering good governance were hallmarks of his government. After inaugurating Pune Metro Line 3 (Pink Line) via video conferencing, Modi said India's operational metro network, which covered 248 km before 2014, now covers 1,200 km, and stressed that better urban infrastructure would accelerate the country's economic growth. The 23-km-long Pink Line, built at a cost of over Rs 8,300 crore, will connect the Hinjewadi IT hub to the District Court Metro station. According to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires list, Ambani's wealth increased by 7.85 per cent, or USD 6.3 billion, making him the biggest gainer globally in the latest update to the ranking on November 2. The gain was substantially ahead of the second-biggest wealth accretion on the list, with Spanish retail billionaire Amancio Ortega adding USD 1.7 billion, followed by China's Zhong Shanshan at USD 1.5 billion. The gains pushed Ambani to No.23 spot on the world billionaire list, making him the richest Indian ahead of Gautam Adani, who was ranked at No.26 with a wealth of USD 79.12 billion, according to the Forbes listing. bf5ea52deba87aaa.title: IPO fundraising rises 30% to record ₹84,400 crore in H1FY27: Report
bf5ea52deba87aaa.summary: India's mainboard IPO market witnessed a record fund mobilisation at Rs 84,400 crore in the first half of FY27, registering a 30 per cent rise over the year-ago period, with nearly 94 per cent of the funds raised during the July-September period, according to a report by Grant Thornton Bharat. As many as 71 companies made their stock market debut during April-September 2026, compared with 55 in the corresponding period a year ago. According to the report, the funds raised increased from Rs 64,900 crore in H1 FY26 to Rs 84,400 crore in H1 FY27. The average listing-day gains improved to 18 per cent from 10 per cent a year ago, while average retail oversubscription increased to 28 times from 25 times, the report titled 'India IPO Market: H1 FY27 and Q2 FY27 Review' said. Notably, September was the busiest month, with 32 IPOs collectively raising Rs 40,400 crore. In terms of sectoral contribution, financial services accounted for 43 per cent of the total capital mobilised during H1 FY

92e91ead481f85e3.title: Amit Shah backs SIR, alleges 3 crore ‘illegal infiltrators’ identified in 13 crore deleted voters
92e91ead481f85e3.summary: Updated - November 03, 2026 01:48 am IST - HYDERABAD Union Home Minister Amit Shah addresses a public meeting during the ‘Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy’ campaign in Hyderabad on Monday (November 2). | Photo Credit: RAMAKRISHNA G Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Monday alleged that the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise had identified around three crore ‘unaccounted voters’, whom he described as ‘illegal infiltrators from Bangladesh’, among the 13 crore names removed from electoral rolls. He asserted that all such infiltrators would be expelled from the country. Addressing a public meeting at MJ Market in Hyderabad’s Old City after a ‘Save democracy-Remove anarchy’ foot march , Mr. Shah claimed that of the nearly 13 crore names deleted from voter lists during the SIR process, 4.25 crore voters were registered in two different locations, three crore were deceased, and another one crore were duplicate entries. He questioned if such names should continue to remain on the electoral rolls. “Do we need to remove infiltrators from the country’s voter lists or not?” he asked. The Home Minister accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of defending the alleged three crore ‘unaccounted’ voters. “No matter how hard Rahul Gandhi or Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy may try, the BJP is committed to driving every infiltrator out of the country,” he said. Mr. Shah alleged that the Congress and other Opposition parties were opposing the SIR exercise to protect ‘infiltrators from Bangladesh’, whom he described as their ‘vote bank’ and maintained that only genuine Indian citizens should be included in electoral rolls. Ridiculing Sunday’s joint rally of Opposition parties in New Delhi, Mr. Shah described it as a ‘Save Infiltrators’ rally and urged BJP workers to counter what he termed ‘fear-mongering’ by the former on the SIR exercise through a door-to-door campaign. The Congress was determined to halt SIR while the BJP would continue to support it

b850f1e5733062c8.title: Petronet LNG reports 52.3% growth in net profits, in talks for availing undelivered cargoes
b850f1e5733062c8.summary: Published - November 03, 2026 05:43 am IST Petronet LNG declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share. | Photo Credit: The Hindu State-owned Petronet LNG reported 53.2% growth in net profits in the September-end quarter, driven by improved operational efficiency, although cargoes from its most prominent supplier, Qatar, continued to be affected because of the reignited conflict in West Asia. The company also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share. The country’s largest LNG importer’s net profit stood at ₹1,235 crore in the reported quarter against ₹806 crore in the same period last year. Revenue from operations although declined about 35% during the period to ₹7,200.35 crore. The company processed 231 trillion British Thermal Units (TBTU) during the period, higher than 228 TBTU it processed in the same period last year. Overall capacity utilisation in the reported quarter narrowed to 64% against 78% in the same period last year. Capacity utilisation at their Dahej terminal stood at 73% against 92% in the comparable period last year. Speaking to the press, Akshay Kumar Singh, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) informed that the company was also in talks with QatarEnergy to secure delivery of the cargoes that could not be delivered because of the force majeure. “On the sidelines, we also discuss if they would be able to give more cargoes before the contractual date. If there is a requirement in the country, we will take that as well,” he said. The supplier has declared forced majeure until December-end. Mr. Singh told reporters that the contractual terms have provisions to recoup the lost cargoes for one year after the expiry of the current contract period, that is, May 2028. He stated that Petronet LNG lost an average 9-10 cargoes each month in the last eight months, thus, about 75-80 cargoes whilst it has received 6 cargoes from the supplier. 63144a20885888e1.title: Fifty years ago | Soviet Cars for Malaysia
63144a20885888e1.summary: Published - November 03, 2026 04:06 am IST SINGAPORE, Nov. 2.: The Soviet Union might assemble its cars in Malaysia and was now seeking to export Moskvich cars to the country, the Soviet Ambassador in Kuala Lumpur, Mr. Bendryshev, said last weekend. All plans for import of cars were ready and only the Government’s license was required, he added. “We have got the technical equipment, diesel engines, aircraft and ships to name a few for export,” he said. The Soviet Union was keen on co-operating with Malaysia to help it to implement its Third Plan by supplying technical expertise and equipment. It was willing to help in energy producing projects, deepening fishing port construction and irrigation projects, he said. Trade expansion and economic co-operation with foreign countries were in line with Russia’s latest five-year plan to produce more goods for export. 478c19867d6818b6.title: Cyclonic storm Murasu to make landfall close to Ongole
478c19867d6818b6.summary: Updated - November 03, 2026 02:42 am IST - VIJAYAWADA A satellite image of Cyclone Murasu over the Bay of Bengal on Sunday. IMD | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement As the cyclonic storm, Cyclone Murasu , moves towards the A.P. coast, the State has deployed six National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and seven State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams in districts likely to be affected by the cyclone. According to information from the A.P. State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA), the landfall point is likely to be Ongole and in this connection, two teams each have been stationed in the districts of Krishna, Bapatla, Guntur, Nellore and Prakasam, while one team each has been deployed in Markapuram, Palnadu and Tirupati districts. Additional teams are also available for deployment if required. Murasu is the second cyclonic storm to hit A.P. in less than a week. According to the 9 p.m. bulletin from the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the cyclonic storm centred over Southwest and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal at 5.30 p.m. It was located about 420 km east-southeast of Chennai, 490 km east-southeast of Nellore, 500 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 510 east-southeast of Kavali, 530 km southeast of Ongole and 560 km south-southeast of Vishakhapatnam. The IMD said the system may intensify further into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over Westcentral Bay of Bengal in the early hours of November 2. The landfall will be close to the Ongole coast, with a wind speed of 100 to 120 kmph, in the early hours of November 3. Isolated extremely heavy rainfall is expected at one or two locations in the districts of Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, Markapuram and Nellore on Monday. NTR and Guntur districts have announced holidays for all government and private schools, junior colleges and degree colleges on Monday (November 2, 2026). 9c21bc940db95f10.title: US judge dismisses Trump admin lawsuit against Harvard over admissions data
9c21bc940db95f10.summary: A federal judge on Monday dismissed a lawsuit against Harvard University over its alleged failure to provide admissions records that the Justice Department had demanded to ensure the Ivy League school stopped using affirmative action in admissions. The Justice Department said Harvard had "thwarted" efforts to investigate potential discrimination. It accused Harvard of refusing to comply with a federal investigation and asked a judge to order the university to turn over the records. But US District Judge Myong Joun concluded that the Justice Department didn't take the necessary procedural steps to obtain the data before filing the lawsuit. "Before taking enforcement action under the statutory framework, the agency must advise the recipient of its failure to comply and determine that compliance cannot be secured by voluntary means," Joun wrote. Giri The Craft Council of Andhra Pradesh (CCAP) inaugurated ‘Vasantham’, an exhibition showcasing the rich heritage of handlooms, handicrafts and traditional crafts of India, in Vijayawada on Monday. Heritage Foods executive director Nara Brahmani visited the exhibition and interacted with the weavers and artisans, and appreciated the efforts of the Craft Council of A.P. in organising the exhibition. She also commended the initiative for providing a valuable platform to weavers and artisans to showcase their products, reach customers and promote their traditional crafts. She said that such exhibitions were extremely beneficial in supporting the weaving community and encouraging the preservation of our rich craft heritage. The two-day exhibition will conclude on November 3 (Tuesday). It remains open from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. at Sesha Sai Kalyana Mandapam, Vedika in the city. e9958b1c4de528c6.title: Police foil bid to snatch smuggled gold from woman at Karipur
e9958b1c4de528c6.summary: Updated - November 03, 2026 08:23 am IST File photo for representational purpose only. The police foiled an attempt to abduct a woman carrying 817 gm gold worth over ₹1.10 crore at Calicut International Airport, Karipur, on Monday. They also arrested two members of the alleged robbery gang. According to the police, the incident took place around 3 a.m. A police team noticed a group behaving suspiciously in the arrival area and kept them under watch. The group followed Abhirami, 27, a native of Vandanmedu in Idukki, after she arrived from abroad. When Abhirami reached the parking area with a man who had come to receive her, the gang blocked their way and grabbed her trolley bag. The police team intervened when the gang tried to overpower the man accompanying her. During the struggle, the accused attacked the police and bit home guard Murali Krishna. They also tried to run over a member of the police team with a car while escaping. The officer narrowly escaped from being hit. The police arrested Sayanth, 28, and Babilesh, 40, both from Kallachi, Nadapuram. Abhirami and Harshal, 40, a native of Kochi who had arrived to collect the gold, were also taken into custody. The police said the gold had been sent with Abhirami by Swalih, a native of Thamarassery. Around 10 people had reached the airport in two cars to seize the gold and abduct her. A search of Abhirami’s baggage led to the recovery of 14 gold plates concealed inside an emergency lamp. The gold weighed 817 gm after cleaning and is estimated to be worth more than ₹1.10 crore. The gold, along with ₹67,000 allegedly kept to pay Abhirami for carrying it, a car and the two people detained in connection with the gold, were handed over to the Customs Department for further action. The police said the arrested men had been involved in several similar cases. One of them had lost a hand in a blast. b7ebb6640bbe2a16.title: US Supreme Court rejects Trump admin's push to set aside California ballots
b7ebb6640bbe2a16.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday rejected a push for California to set aside thousands of mail ballots from people President Donald Trump's administration claims are noncitizens, a decision that comes on the eve of the pivotal midterm elections. The high court refused to intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state's voter rolls. It was the latest in a flurry of election-related litigation the day before the midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress for the last two years of Trump's second term. In California, the Trump administration had asked the high court to set aside the challenged ballots until the voters' citizenship status could be verified. But officials there said that the list appeared to be filled with errors and that setting the ballots aside could effectively disenfranchise legal voters. The high court did not detail its reasoning, as is common in emergency decisions.

ec05d0c73acf6bca.title: Netanyahu presses Trump for fresh Iran strikes after US midterm elections
ec05d0c73acf6bca.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday's midterm elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter. A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week's elections. US President Donald Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes while pushing for a deal with Iran. The two officials said diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. The two officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the US lifting its blockade on Iran's ports. They said more talks are planned for this week. The two officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were discussing classified briefing

f5c1503860f7f7db.title: Cascading effect: On dams and land rights
f5c1503860f7f7db.summary: Published - November 03, 2026 12:56 am IST The bureaucratic impetus for the 11.2-GW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh purportedly comes from China’s aggressive development of a 60-GW mega-dam in Tibet , stoking anxieties among Indian authorities over ‘weaponised’ transboundary waters. Beijing may be able to divert flows in the Yarlung Tsangpo river, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, to cause drought downstream or release water en masse to trigger catastrophic floods in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. New Delhi thus imagines SUMP as a strategic buffer, but in so doing faces a dilemma it should not attempt to resolve with force. Its extant top-down approach, exemplified by deploying security forces to guard survey teams and imposing the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against activists, only validates fears among locals that the state will grab their land. The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. The eastern Himalayas are among the most tectonically active and erosion-prone landscapes in the world. The mega-dam in Tibet will comprise five cascading power stations over the river’s roughly 2,000-metre fall over 50 km. Beijing has maintained the dam will not harm countries downstream but has declined to share crucial engineering details. This is why diplomacy will be an essential part of operating SUMP, in addition to Beijing’s disputed claims on Arunachal Pradesh. The Brahmaputra basin in Assam and Bangladesh receives most of its water from monsoon rains and tributaries downstream of the Tibetan Plateau, so China cannot straightforwardly control the river’s total flow through India. b728e7f1ff8873f6.title: Cyclone Murasu crosses Andhra coast, leaves a heavy trail of destruction
b728e7f1ff8873f6.summary: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu began its landfall process close to Ongole in Prakasam district in the early hours of Wednesday, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. According to the Met department, the cyclone started making landfall around 1 am on Wednesday, bringing heavy rainfall, accompanied by gale winds reaching speeds of up to 110 kmph and gusting up to 120 kmph. "The landfall process commenced at 0100 hours IST on November 3. The forward sector of the wall cloud is entering the coast, while the wall cloud region is very close to the coast," the IMD's official press release said. Under the influence of the cyclone, heavy rain struck several places in the southern state. The cyclone was centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal, close to the South Andhra Pradesh coast, about 40 km southeast of Ongole, 60 km northeast of Kavali and 70 km south of Bapatla, as of 0130 hours. The IMD said the landfall point was expected to be between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ong

It had clocked a net profit of Rs 222.05 crore in the second quarter of the preceding financial year, the company said in an exchange filing. During the second quarter of FY27, the company's total income, however, increased to Rs 5,958.24 crore from Rs 5,585.21 crore in the year-ago period. 6fe4e482fbc13805.title: A hundred years ago | Tutankh-Amen’s Tomb: Contents of the Second Chamber
6fe4e482fbc13805.summary: Published - November 03, 2026 03:57 am IST CAIRO, Nov. 2.: The newspaper Siasash learns from a trustworthy source that the contents of the third chamber of Tutankh-Amen’s tomb have recently been opened and while they are not so rich and fine as those of the other two chambers they are of great historical importance, because they represent everything used for the funeral ceremony. Thirty small boats of two kinds were found, one sort being that used for funerals for journeying from Luxor across the Nile to the tombs and the other sort intended to transport the body from the earth to heaven. A very interesting box of small statuettes has also been found having Tutankh-Amen’s head but the body of a bird or animal, giving the Egyptian conception after life and two chariots have been found unornamented. They were supposed to have been used during hunting. These are the first of their kind ever discovered. 729df165de669f2f.title: Mangala sloka for Rama
729df165de669f2f.summary: Published - November 03, 2026 04:50 am IST When Valmiki saw a hunter kill one of a pair of krauncha birds, he cursed the hunter through a sloka. But the sloka can also be interpreted differently, in a positive sense, said M.A. Venkatakrishnan in a discourse. Valmiki’s sloka begins with the word manishadah . If you split this as ma and nishada , then it is Valmiki addressing the hunter ( nishada ). Valmiki curses the hunter, “Oh hunter! You killed one of two birds which were making love ( kaamamohitam ). Because of that, you will never have any peace.” But if the word manishadah is not split, then it means the One who is never separated from ma , that is Mahalakshmi. So, this can be taken as a reference to Rama Himself. While the words shasvathi samah pratistham tvam agamah have a negative meaning when we take them as referring to the hunter, they also can mean ‘May you live long.’ Kaamamohitam can be seen as a reference to Ravana, who was caught in kama (lust) for Sita. So, the entire sloka can be seen as a mangala sloka for Rama, the One who is never separated from Sita and the One who killed the lustful asura. While Valmiki’s intention was to curse the hunter, it so happened that he presented the Ramayana story in a nutshell through that sloka. There are certain rules to be followed while writing a kavya . A mahakavya must have thousands of verses, and Valmiki’s Ramayana has 24,000 verses. Although many versions of the Ramayana came up later, Valmiki’s is the authentic account, because he was witness to everything that happened in Rama’s life, thanks to the divine vision which Brahma gave him. When Lord Narayana decided to take the Rama avatara, Veda Purusha decided to take an avatara as Valmiki Ramayana. So, the Ramayana is the embodiment of Vedic tenets. It has many tattvas which need deep study and analysis. Published - November 03, 2026 04:50 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 0056552907126bc0.title: Bajaj Auto's total sales during October rise 14% to 591,876 units
0056552907126bc0.summary: Bajaj Auto on Monday posted a 14 per cent year-on-year growth in its total sales during October, with double-digit growth across two-wheelers and commercial vehicles. The automaker's total wholesales stood at 5,91,876 units, against 5,18,170 units in the year-ago period, according to an exchange filing. Domestic sales rose 12 per cent to 3,51,148 units, while exports grew 18 per cent to 2,40,728 units. Total two-wheeler sales increased by 13 per cent to 5,01,194 units from 4,42,316 in the year-ago period. Total commercial vehicle sales were higher by 20 per cent to 90,682 units, compared to 75,854 units. Bajaj Auto's total sales during the April-October period rose 22 per cent to 35,79,011 units. Palaniswami on Monday expressed concern over the previous month’s reported three per cent growth in the Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections in Tamil Nadu, which was much below the national average. In a post on his social media handle, Mr. Palaniswami referred to the State’s level of inflation which was higher than that of the all-India figure and “diversion” of industrial projects to other States, similar to what was shown in a feature film of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. “How would the GST collections go up unless industry achieved progress, which would, in turn, generate jobs; enable higher growth in Gross Domestic Production and rise in per capita income?” Mr. Palaniswami wondered. Recalling that the Guidance Tamil Nadu, the nodal agency for investment promotion and single-window facilitation, was established when Jayalalithaa was Chief Minister, the AIADMK leader accused the present TVK-led government of having “ruined” it. e21b19eda890a1b1.title: Telangana plans AI-enabled transactions in agri. market yards
e21b19eda890a1b1.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:51 pm IST - HYDERABAD Minister for Agriculture Tummala Nageswara Rao holding a meeting with marketing officials in Hyderabad on Monday. | Photo Credit: By Arrangement The Telangana government is planning to make the agricultural markets in the State AI (artificial intelligence)-enabled for the first time in the country and also make them model markets, Minister for Agriculture Tummala Nageswara Rao said. At a meeting with the agricultural marketing and agriculture departments here on Monday, he said the AI technology would check for irregularities in transactions in market yards. Tenders for introduction of AI technology in the market yards’ transactions would be called within a week. He suggested them to bring into a single digital system all transactions related to farmers — from the farmer entering the market with his/her produce, its sale, payments and others till he/she leaves the market yard. Listing of farmers’ details, allocation of identity number to every lot/crop, assessing crop quality, fixing price, digital bidding/tender details, online auction, farmer’s consent, weighing, sale bills, market charges, payments to farmers, recording of gate exit, e-receipts and e-permits issuance should be done on a single platform. The management information system should also have details of commission agents, traders, price patterns, auction details and others so that they can be cross-checked in future too. The Minister told the officials to study the digital marketing systems being implemented elsewhere in the country. Even the attendance of marketing department officials, including biometric attendance registering, be also made part of the new digital system. The market yards should also have closed-circuit camera systems to monitor maintenance of godowns and daily activities. Digital screens also be arranged so that farmers could know about the prices elsewhere in the country. On the Koheda integrated fruit market, the Minister ask

ff536a96e0fae5ce.title: CPI(M) seeks action against Pendurthi MLA over alleged irregular voting in GVMC polls
ff536a96e0fae5ce.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:45 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM The Communist Party of India (Marxist) on Monday petitioned the District Collector, seeking legal action against Pendurthi MLA Panchakarla Ramesh Babu and the concerned polling officials over an alleged irregularity in the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) elections held on November 1. In a representation, party district secretary M. Jaggunaidu alleged that Mr. Ramesh Babu voted for the mayoral and corporator candidates at Booth No. 115/8 in Ward 115, where, he claimed, the MLA had no vote. He further alleged that the booth officials issued ballot papers to the MLA in violation of election law, and contended that such conduct would erode public confidence in the electoral process. The party leaders demanded a thorough enquiry and action against the legislator and concerned officials. According to the leaders, complaints were submitted to the State Election Commissioner and the Returning Officers of the GVMC Pendurthi zone. 88523712e648304f.title: Joint survey to resolve Revenue-Forest land disputes: Ponguleti
88523712e648304f.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:43 pm IST - HYDERABAD Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy at a review meeting with Revenue, Forest and Survey and Settlement officials at the Secretariat on Monday. The Telangana government has decided to undertake joint surveys by the Revenue and Forest departments to find a permanent solution to long-pending disputes over land boundaries, particularly those involving forest, revenue and patta lands. Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy directed officials of both departments to work in close coordination and ensure that ordinary people and farmers do not suffer because of inter-departmental boundary disputes. At a review meeting with Revenue, Forest and Survey and Settlement officials at the Secretariat, the Minister said the government, under the leadership of Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, was committed to resolving land-related issues that had remained unsettled for decades. Pointing out that the erstwhile Khammam, Warangal and Adilabad districts had substantial forest areas, Mr. Ponguleti said boundary disputes between the Revenue and Forest departments had persisted for several decades. He called for scientific and technology-based joint surveys to establish clear boundaries and prevent such disputes from recurring. Officials should examine the actual ground position and comprehensively reconcile land records, maps and survey details before arriving at conclusions. Issues that could be settled at the field level should be resolved locally, while matters requiring higher-level intervention should be referred to the State government without delay, he said. Observing that prolonged disputes had caused considerable hardship to farmers and landowners, he said he would personally monitor the joint survey exercise and periodically review its progress. ecee93d69cbdb6d7.title: One held in Keralam for securing job in panchayat with fake mark list
ecee93d69cbdb6d7.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:39 pm IST - PALAKKAD Representational image. | Photo Credit: Getty Images A former Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) unit secretary was arrested for allegedly securing a contractual job at Puthukkode grama panchayat here by submitting a fake BCom mark list. The arrested person, K.V. Ganapathy, a native of Puthukkode Kizhakke Gramam, worked as an accountant-cum-IT assistant in the panchayat’s employment guarantee scheme section. The Vadakkenchery police arrested him in connection with the case on Monday. Mr. Ganapathy joined the panchayat on a contractual basis in July 2021, when the Left Democratic Front (LDF) was in power. He continued in the post until July 2026. He had submitted a BCom mark list purportedly issued by the University of Calicut as proof of his educational qualification. After the United Democratic Front (UDF) came to power in the last local body elections, the panchayat committee refused to extend his contract. Mr. Ganapathy then approached the High Court and obtained an order allowing him to continue in the post until September 2026. The alleged fraud came to light during the verification process for his reinstatement. The new panchayat administration became suspicious because Mr. Ganapathy had submitted only a mark list, rather than an original or provisional degree certificate, to prove his qualification. Growing suspicious, the panchayat authorities sent the mark list to the University of Calicut for verification. The university informed them that the document was fake and that Mr. Ganapathy had not passed the BCom degree. 53c883e3af2a990d.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:39 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA The State Election Commission (SEC) has made arrangements for the counting of votes in 92 urban local bodies (13 Municipal Corporations and 79 Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats) from 8 a.m. on November 3 (Tuesday). SEC Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha, in a press release, said that counting was being conducted for a total of 3,186 wards, including 804 in Municipal Corporations (MCs) and 2,382 in Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats (M&NPs). The total number of counting centres is 138 — 22 in Municipal Corporations and the remaining in Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats. The counting process will be undertaken by 47,817 supervisors, assistants and staff (28,182 in MCs and 19,635 in M&NPs). A total of 1,372 CCTVs have been installed at strong rooms and counting centres (98 in MCs and 126 in M&NPs). Meanwhile, the SEC reported that the final voting percentage in the 92 urban local bodies that went to polls on November 1 stood at 62.16, with 60,22,411 of the 96,89,061 voters exercising their franchise. 1e06532f2305d2f6.title: TG-Redco for speeding up implementation of renewable energy schemes
1e06532f2305d2f6.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:33 pm IST - HYDERABAD Vice-chairman and MD of TG-Redco Jithesh V. Patil holding a virtual meeting with district managers from Hyderabad on Monday. | Photo Credit: Arrangement Vice-chairman and managing director of the Telangana State Renewable Energy Development Corporation (TG-Redco) Jithesh V. Patil has asked officials to accelerate the implementation of renewable energy schemes across the State and achieve planned targets within stipulated timelines. In a virtual meeting held on Monday with the district managers of the Redco, he stressed the need to identify field-level challenges and resolve them promptly through coordination with the departments concerned. He reviewed the Model Solar Village Programme, installation of rooftop solar power plants, solarisation of agricultural pump sets, PM-KUSUM scheme, energy conservation activities and development of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure. He sought details from the officials on the work completed so far, current status and pending issues. Mr. Patil told the district managers to create awareness among eligible consumers about the benefits of rooftop solar under the Gruha Jyothi scheme. He called for district-level action plans to achieve the targets under agricultural pump set solarisation and the PM-KUSUM scheme. On pending approvals and inspections, he instructed officials to speed up the process of obtaining necessary approvals from various departments and complete pending inspections without delay. 6514719c07d112bf.title: Madurai medico detained in Russia for 10 days returns home after MP’s intervention
6514719c07d112bf.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:37 pm IST - MADURAI A 21-year-old medical student from Madurai, who was trapped in a Russian detention facility for 10 days amid flight cancellations caused by ongoing war tensions, has returned safely to her hometown following the intervention of Madurai Member of Parliament Su. Venkatesan. Daisy Asha Moraes, a fourth-year student at the South Ural State Medical University in Russia, had planned to return to India on leave for medical reasons. With her visa set to expire on October 20, she booked a flight via Moscow and arrived at the airport on October 18. However, ongoing drone attacks linked to the Russia-Ukraine conflict forced the cancellation of domestic flights, grounding her scheduled journey. When alternative flights failed to materialise immediately, Russian authorities detained her under the classification of overstaying her expired visa, initiating detention proceedings on October 20. Although a local court granted a 10-day grace period, her family faced mounting anxiety that she could be held in detention for up to 90 days. After exhausting other avenues, the student’s father, Arul Moraes, sought the assistance of Mr. Venkatesan. Operating through parliamentary offices in Madurai and New Delhi, Mr. Venkatesan’s team coordinated directly with the External Affairs Minister, senior ministry officials, and the Indian Embassy in Russia. Compiling documentation regarding her medical condition and the war-related flight disruptions, officials presented the case to Russian authorities on October 27, establishing that the student bore no fault in the travel disruption. Originally informed that the student could not leave until November 15, the intervention successfully expedited her departure. Medical assistance and travel arrangements were secured, and Moraes boarded a flight to India on November 1, arriving safely in Madurai. e3eb50752922ec13.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:36 pm IST - HYDERABAD Roads and Buildings Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy at a review meeting with senior officials at the Secretariat on Monday. The 85th Indian Roads Congress (IRC) summit, scheduled to be held in Hyderabad from November 19 to 22, should be transformed into a global platform to showcase Telangana’s development, culture and investment potential, Roads and Buildings Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy said. At a review meeting with senior officials at the Secretariat on Monday, the Minister directed them to make the event a precursor to the ‘Invest Telangana’ Global Summit scheduled to be held in December at Bharat Future City. He said the IRC summit should not remain confined to technical discussions on roads and infrastructure but should also help attract investments, industries and employment opportunities to the State. Officials should prepare a special action plan to connect with potential investors and encourage them to participate in the December global investment summit. Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari and Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy would jointly inaugurate the four-day summit at HITEX on November 19. Union Ministers, Ministers from various States, senior bureaucrats, international delegates and experts from the engineering and infrastructure sectors are expected to participate. Mr. Komatireddy, who reviewed the arrangements for nearly three-and-a-half hours, asked officials to establish a special ‘Telangana Pavilion’ at the venue to showcase the State’s history, culture, traditions, arts, tourism destinations and major development projects. Around 400 exhibition stalls would be set up as part of the event. 3ce124ce86c16ef5.title: Chittoor, Annamayya districts brace for Cyclone Murasu
3ce124ce86c16ef5.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:34 pm IST - CHITTOOR/MADANAPALLE The officials are prepared for any emergency following a high alert for Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu across South Andhra Pradesh, projected to impact Chittoor and Annamayya districts over the next 48 hours. While the core system is projected to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, the sprawling outer bands of the cyclone are expected to reach the interior Rayalaseema region. Officials have issued an orange alert for Chittoor district, warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall through Monday and Tuesday. Neighbouring Annamayya district, which began the week under a yellow warning, is bracing for an escalation to an orange alert on Tuesday, with expectations of downpours in isolated areas. Officials said that the sudden rain could trigger severe waterlogging in low-lying tracts, spill over swollen streams, and trigger localised flooding in vulnerable rural pockets. Farmers across the Nagari, Chittoor, and Palamaner revenue divisions in Chittoor district and the eastern parts of Annamayya district initiated measures to protect standing paddy, horticultural orchards, and vegetable plots from gusty winds and floodwaters. Officials of the APSPDCL and civic officials were instructed to be prepared in the event of potential snapping of power lines and major roadblocks caused by uprooted trees. Annamayya district Collector Nishant Kumar said that with the crucial 48-hour window under way, the district machinery has swung into action at all vulnerable areas. “Revenue, police, municipal, and disaster response teams remain stationed on high alert in flood-prone zones,” he said. Chittoor Collector Sumit Kumar said that the district administration has issued strict advisories urging residents to stay alert to official weather bulletins. “Above all, the public should be cautious about fast-flowing streams and causeways,” he said. a14467189d646d17.title: Telangana Civil Supplies officials uncover rice sale violations, hoarding in Hyderabad
a14467189d646d17.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:35 pm IST - HYDERABAD Diversion of rice meant for Public Distribution System (PDS) was one of the violation detected by Telangana Civil Supplies teams during checks between October 29 and 31. The image is used for representative purposes only. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT Telangana Civil Supplies Department officials uncovered violations in sale of rice at a few outlets in Hyderabad and Rangareddy districts. The violations include weight manipulations by traders by affixing 26-kilogram labels onto bags having only 25 kilograms of rice , and exorbitant prices pasted over the rates printed by manufacturers. The department’s teams lodged complaints at Saroornagar, Jeedimetla, and Alwal police stations, based on which action was initiated, as per official information. This follows surprise checks by the Enforcement Task Force (ETF) along with the Legal Metrology Department across Hyderabad and Ranga Reddy districts between October 29 to 31. The other violations detected include diversion and hoarding of Public Distribution System (PDS) rice, traders operating without mandatory trade, GST, Labour, or FSSAI licenses. The teams have documented the offences on-site by taking videos and photos. The department stated that the vigilance will continue. The State government on Saturday (October 31, 2026) announced a ceiling on maximum retail price (MRP) on three varieties of fine rice in the urban limits , which are most consumed by people. As per the orders, price of a kg of BPT/KNM variety was fixed at ₹66; RNR/Telangana Sona at ₹74 and HMT/JSR variety at ₹79, in Hyderabad and Medchal. d4535bfeee0e14e6.title: Pawan Kalyan directs high alert as Cyclone Murasu nears Nellore coast
d4535bfeee0e14e6.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:38 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan | Photo Credit: File photo Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan has directed officials to remain on high alert as cyclone Murasu approaches the coast, even as the State is yet to recover from the damage caused by cyclone Arnab. At a review meeting with senior officials of the Panchayat Raj and Rural Development and Rural Water Supply Departments on Monday, Mr. Kalyan said the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had warned of extremely heavy rain in Nellore, Prakasam, Markapuram, Bapatla and Krishna districts. In view of the forecast of intense rainfall, he stressed the need to evacuate people living in low-lying areas to safer locations, ensure proper coordination among departments, minimise hardship and prevent loss of life. Officials informed the Deputy Chief Minister that the cyclone was initially forecast to cross the coast between Bapatla and Machilipatnam. However, it had changed course and was now expected to make landfall near Nellore. Heavy rain was already lashing Nellore, Prakasam, Bapatla, Tirupati and Markapuram districts under the influence of the cyclone. Six National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and seven State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams had been kept on standby, officials said. They added that other necessary precautionary measures were being taken. Hitendra | Photo Credit: File photo The High Court of Karnataka on Monday nominated Additional Director General of Police (ADGP) R. Hitendra as the new head of the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing criminal cases related to alleged illegalities in the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC), in place of DGP Alok Kumar. Mr. Hitendra is currently serving as ADGP (Law and Order) at the police headquarters in Bengaluru. Meanwhile, the court nominated another ADGP, Soumendu Mukherjee, currently serving as ADGP (Administration), as a member of the SIT in place of Diya Gopinathan, who is posted as Director of the Forensic Sciences Laboratory. Justice M. Nagaprasanna passed the order while modifying the September 21 order constituting the SIT, in terms of the direction of the apex court, which had asked the High Court to replace Mr. Kumar and Ms. Gopinathan. The apex court had passed the order on an appeal filed by the State government challenging the setting up of the SIT by the High Court. However, the apex court had upheld the High Court’s decision to constitute the SIT but accepted certain reservations expressed by the State government over the nomination of Mr. Kumar to the SIT. The apex court had also found merit in the government’s contention that Ms. Gopinathan’s nomination to the SIT could result in a conflict of interest when the SIT refers investigation materials to the FSL for examination. The apex court had left it to the High Court to reconstitute the SIT while giving liberty to the government to suggest to the High Court names of senior police officers not below the rank of ADGP to replace Mr. Kumar and Ms. Gopinathan. Meanwhile, the High Court directed the State government not to transfer members of the SIT out of Bengaluru till the completion of the investigation. 8d7756523fa00748.title: Residents seek closure of Tasmac outlet, illegal recreation club in Keela Arasadi panchayat
8d7756523fa00748.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:43 pm IST - THOOTHUKUDI: Residents of Thuppaspatti and Ayyanarpuram at the Collectorate in Thoothukudi on Monday. | Photo Credit: N. RAJESH Residents of Thuppaspatti and Ayyanarpuram in the district on Monday submitted a petition to the Collector, seeking closure of a newly opened Tasmac outlet and an ‘llegal’ recreation club nearby. The petition was submitted at the weekly grievance redressal meeting chaired by Collector Vishu Mahajan. In their petition, the villagers said the Tasmac outlet and the club in Thuppaspatti-Ayyanarpuram area under Keela Arasadi panchayat were causing several problems. Also, while staging continuous protests demanding the closure of both outlets, anti-social elements were issuing death threats to the protesters. The petitioners said that drunken people made it a regular practice to engage in quarrels in nearby thickets, break and throw liquor bottles and lie around in an intoxicated state. This raised serious safety concerns among women, who left for work at the salt pans early in the morning, and school students passing through the area. The residents urged the authorities to permanently shut down the Tasmac outlet and the recreation club, which were causing inconvenience to the public, and take stringent action against those threatening and intimidating the villagers. In a separate petition, Sudalai of Meelavittan and other villagers said that 70 goats died after allegedly consuming wastewater discharged from a fertilizer godown owned by a private company at Veeranayakkanthattu near Thoothukudi. The animals had been grazing in the area. They sought criminal action against the godown management and adequate compensation for the loss of goats. 668d07ff7e0eaaea.title: Ranji Trophy: Urvil and Vishal boost Gujarat
668d07ff7e0eaaea.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:37 pm IST - Ahmedabad Opener Aarya hit six fours and three maximums in his 95. | Photo Credit: VIJAY SONEJI A frustratingly familiar script unfolded again for Kerala at the Narendra Modi stadium here on Monday. For the third time this season, Kerala allowed the opposition’s lower-order to fight back and wrest away the hard-earned advantage. An unbeaten, counterattacking 111-run partnership for the sixth wicket between Urvil Patel (63 batting, 67b, 7x4, 1x6) and Vishal Jayswal (50 batting, 83b, 3x4, 2x6) was the latest to hurt Kerala as Gujarat ended the opening day of the Ranji Trophy Elite Group C match at 300 for five. Soon after tea, Kerala had Gujarat in a spot of bother at 189 for five when Jaymeet Patel (one) was stumped by Mohammed Azharuddeen off Aditya Sarvate. But the visiting side let Gujarat off the hook when it failed to grab the chances and wilted under the calculated assault by Urvil and Vishal. Rohan Kunnummal showed poor judgement while running back and failed to reach a skier from Vishal off Vaisakh Chandran when the batter was on 33. Azharuddeen fumbled when Urvil, on 32, stepped out to attack Sarvate. Urvil and Vishal capitalised on these errors to take their side to a position of strength in the final session. Earlier, Kerala had crawled back into the contest in the post-lunch session, picking up four wickets to reduce the host to 182 for four. The strikes included that of top-scorer Aarya Desai (95, 132b, 6x4, 3x6), who in a hurry to reach his hundred top-edged a wild slog and was caught by Vishnu Vinod off Vaisakh. In the morning, openers Aarya and Abhishek Desai played fluently against the Kerala bowlers who found little help from the track. However, a better disciplined show with the ball in the second session choked the flow runs which forced the Gujarat batters to take the risks, which ultimately led to their downfall. The scores: Gujarat — 1st innings: Abhishek Desai c Rohan b Nidheesh 42, Aarya Desai c Vi

8cbf0812f433ba6c.title: Namakkal farmers oppose the proposed Sankari-Vellakoil NH project
8cbf0812f433ba6c.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:52 pm IST - Namakkal The farmers in Namakkal have opposed upgrading the two-lane highway at Padaiveedu to a four-lane road under the proposed Sankari–Vellakoil NH 381A project. | Photo Credit: LAKSHMI NARAYANAN E Farmers in Namakkal district have opposed the proposed Sankari-Vellakoil national highway project 381A and want it implemented on alternate routes. The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has proposed a 70-km inter-corridor highway connecting NH 81 in Tiruppur district to NH 544 near Sankari in Salem district. The project cost is estimated at ₹ 2,000 crore and the four-way lane is expected to pass through about 19 km in Namakkal district. Farmers have raised opposition, stating that the project would severely affect farmlands, schools, spinning mills, and houses. P. Perumal, general secretary of the Tamil Nadu Vivasayigal Sangam, said the project starts at Padaiveedu town panchayat in Namakkal district and passes through Sowdapuram, Patharai, Pallipalayam Agraharam, Elanthakuttai, Kadachanallur, and Pappampalayam panchayats before entering Erode district. The project envisions laying 150-ft road for 19 km in Namakkal district. This would affect around 200 acres of farmland, schools at Padaiveedu, Uppupalayam, spinning mills, and over 100 houses. Likewise, 18 village roads will have to be destroyed for the project. Two weeks ago, farmers from seven villages submitted a petition against the project at the divisional-level farmers’ grievances meet at the Pallipalayam panchayat union office. Now, farmers from Erode and Tiruppur districts are also in talks to organise protests jointly against the proposed project, Mr. Perumal added. Stating that the project would be mostly beneficial for industries and corporates, Mr. Perumal said the proposed road would facilitate easy movement of containers to Thoothukudi through Dharapuram and Madurai. 783e08fb334bc57d.title: PWD employees stage black badge protest over delayed October salary
783e08fb334bc57d.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:52 pm IST - MADURAI Employees of the Tamil Nadu Government Public Works Department Accounts and Administrative Staff Association staged a State-wide protest on Monday, wearing black badges to condemn the non-disbursement of October salary to over a thousand employees across the Public Works Department (PWD) and the Water Resources Department. The salary delay, affecting personnel from chief engineers down to office assistants, has severely impacted livelihoods as the Deepavali festival approaches, said Abdul Najimudeen, general secretary of the association. Association representatives revealed that the delay stemmed from files pending in the Finance Department and the salary item being disabled in the IFHRMS portal, leaving employees unable to receive timely pay even with government intervention. They noted that pay authorisation bottlenecks—with delays recurring every three to six months—and unapproved temporary posts have created major administrative hurdles, echoing a similar crisis last July when salaries were delayed past the 15th of the month. The association has put forward an eight-point charter of demands, urging the State government to disburse salaries immediately on a war footing and find a permanent solution to departmental issues rather than handling staff livelihoods casually. Key demands include issuing requested transfers pending for the last five months, promoting over 450 junior assistants and typists, regularising temporary workers who have served for over a decade, revoking Government Order No. 69, converting divisional accountant posts into a State service, and filling all vacant positions. Warning that this year’s festival risks becoming a ‘black Deepavali’ for PWD staff, the union announced escalated protests if their grievances are ignored. A zonal-level dharna is scheduled for November 17, followed by a massive hunger strike at the Chennai PWD campus on December 8. Published - November 02, 2026 07:23 pm IST Te

e32d6b6853bbb527.title: Facial recognition attendance system introduced as pilot project in SCCL’s Kothagudem Area
e32d6b6853bbb527.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:39 pm IST - BHADRADRI KOTHAGUDEM A facial recognition-based attendance system was introduced on a trial basis in the Kothagudem Area of the Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) on Monday. The initiative is part of the SCCL’s efforts to adopt technology in its employee attendance system to enhance transparency. Biometric attendance systems are already in use at some General Managers’ offices in SCCL. However, this is the first time the system is being implemented across the coal mines and departments of an entire area. The initiative is aimed at promoting discipline and punctuality among employees and is expected to improve transparency and productivity, according to an SCCL press release. SCCL has around 40,000 employees, of whom approximately 1,600 work in the Kothagudem Area. The trial run began in the Kothagudem Area as a pilot project on Monday. The system is expected to be extended to mines and departments in other areas in a phased manner. 8568b14a98d223eb.title: Karnataka deploys 500 linemen, equipment to restore power supply in cyclone-hit Andhra Pradesh
8568b14a98d223eb.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:49 pm IST - Bengaluru The State government is providing contingency funds to meet travel, accommodation and other emergency expenses of the deployed personnel. | Photo Credit: File Photo Karnataka has deployed 500 trained power utility workers and specialised equipment to Andhra Pradesh to help restore electricity infrastructure damaged by Cyclone Arnab. The deployment follows a request from the Andhra Pradesh government for manpower and equipment to carry out restoration work in cyclone-affected areas. The Karnataka government has mobilised the teams under the supervision of Energy Minister K.J. George as part of inter-State cooperation. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar spoke to his Andhra Pradesh counterpart N. Chandrababu Naidu over the phone and assured him of Karnataka’s support. “Electricity is an essential service, and restoring it immediately is necessary for the well-being of people affected by the disaster. Karnataka stands firmly with the people of Andhra Pradesh during this difficult time,” the Chief Minister said. Mr. George said Karnataka’s teams would work closely with Andhra Pradesh officials to restore power supply at the earliest through field-level coordination and the deployment of specialised equipment. The State has sent 500 trained linemen, 15 Palfinger trucks equipped with cranes and earth augers, and 25 tractor-mounted drilling machines. The teams were mobilised on an emergency basis and left for Andhra Pradesh on Monday afternoon, reaching the State by midnight. For effective deployment and coordination, each electricity supply company (ESCOM) has appointed a single-point contact officer to liaise with the concerned Andhra Pradesh officials. The linemen have been divided into teams of 10, each led by a junior or assistant engineer. Annamayya district Collector Nishant Kumar inspected the strong rooms and counting centres in Madanapalle, while Chittoor Collector Sumit Kumar reviewed the arrangements in Chittoor on Monday (November 2). In Sri Sathya Sai district, SP S. Satish Kumar inspected the strong rooms in Dharmavaram and reviewed security arrangements. “Heavy police bandobast has been deployed at counting centres, with special focus on preventing unauthorised entry, maintaining law and order and avoiding clashes between political groups. Strong rooms housing ballot boxes are under round-the-clock security,” said Sumit Kumar. “CCTV surveillance and strict entry regulations will be enforced at counting venues. Candidates and their authorised counting agents only will be allowed inside after verification,” Sri Sathya Sai district Collector A. Shyam Prasad said. a02bb588eee39523.title: Six fishermen safe as fishing boat runs aground at Rushikonda beach in Visakhapatnam
a02bb588eee39523.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:37 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Rescued crew members of the fishing vessel that drifted ashore at Rushikonda beach in Visakhapatnam on Monday. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT A major maritime mishap was averted when a mechanised fishing boat drifted ashore near Rushikonda Beach on Monday, after its engine failed and ran out of fuel in rough seas. All six fishermen aboard the vessel were unharmed as the boat grounded near the shoreline. According to the fisheries officials and coastal police, the fishing boat, bearing registration number IND.AP.V5.MM.255 and owned by Korangi Narsinga Rao, had set out on a routine fishing expedition off the Visakhapatnam coast a few days ago. Trouble began at mid-sea when the vessel’s engine developed a technical snag and subsequently ran out of fuel. The crew dropped anchor in an attempt to stabilise the drifting vessel. However, strong tidal surges and turbulent waves caused by the adverse weather conditions along the coast caused the anchor line to snap. Unable to manoeuver the vessel in the swelling waters, the boat along with the crew was carried westward by high-energy waves before the boat ran aground near Rushikonda beach. Recounting the incident one of the crew members said: “We lost power after running out of fuel, and before we could secure the boat, the anchor broke under heavy wave pressure. Fortunately, the ocean tides pushed us towards the shore rather than towards the deep sea.” Beach lifeguards, local fishermen, and Coastal Security Police quickly rushed to the spot on seeing the grounded vessel. Officials confirmed that all six crew members managed to disembark safely without sustaining injuries. Marine police authorities and fisheries department staff arrived at Rushikonda to inspect the vessel for structural damage and made arrangements to tow it once sea conditions improve. 00d12a7aa8bf2173.title: Tasmac workers shut shops in Namakkal, Salem
00d12a7aa8bf2173.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:49 pm IST - Salem A total of 155 Tasmac outlets in Namakkal and many outlets in Salem downed shutters on Monday, in protest against the implementation of new Environmental and Social Welfare Cess. Meanwhile, on Sunday evening, three customers went to an outlet at Pillur near Paramathi Velur, returned the empty liquor bottles and demanded money. Due to server issues, the bottles could not be scanned and it resulted in a quarrel between the customers and the salesman, Purusothaman (46). During the quarrel, the three men hit Purusothaman with a bottle and he sustained injuries. He was admitted to Paramathi Velur Government Hospital. Similarly, customers attacked another salesman, Marimuthu, at Nallar outlet and damaged his two-wheeler. In Salem district, acting on complaints that Tasmac workers were collecting excess money for bottles, the officials checked an outlet at Venkatappa Chetty Street at Pal Market on Sunday evening. They found the allegations to be true. Following this, the outlet salesmen Senthil, Pachaperumal, and supervisor Govindan were placed under suspension. c051082588990188.title: Villagers stage protest at Collectorate demanding mobile ration shop
c051082588990188.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:35 pm IST - RAMANATHAPURAM Keelakarai villagers staged a demonstration outside the Ramanathapuram Collectorate demanding the setting up of a mobile ration shop. The Collector assured that action will be taken. More than a hundred villagers and members of the women’s self-help group from Velanoor (South) village in Keelakarai taluk, Ramanathapuram district, besieged the Collectorate, demanding the establishment of a mobile ration shop in their village. They then stated that they intended to submit their family cards along with a petition to Collector M. Sivaguru Prabhakaran at the public grievance redressal meeting. After the Collector assured them that appropriate action would be taken, the villagers returned with their family cards. The villagers stated, “There are 210 family cards in our village. We all purchase essential goods from the ration shop operating in Velanoor North Street, which is located one km away. As Scheduled Caste community people, we face various hardships when we go there to buy goods from a ration shop located in an area where people of another community reside. So, we have submitted petitions multiple times to the District Supply Officer to set up a mobile ration shop in our village once a month. On July 7th, we staged a siege protest at the Keelakarai Tahsildar’s office. During the talks held under the chairmanship of the Tahsildar that day, an assurance was given to set up a mobile ration shop. However, no ration shop has been set up to date. Hence, we came to surrender our family cards to the District Collector. The Collector has assured us that action will be taken.” Published - November 02, 2026 07:35 pm IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. India would be without regular skipper Shubman Gill, and his deputy KL Rahul in the last two games as they will begin preparing for the two-match Test series starting November 19. So, I think New Zealand have a slight advantage because you aren't playing the same team in all five matches," Pujara told 'JioStar'. "I'm still backing the Indian team in the first three matches, as I feel they will do well. The last two matches could be a bit of a challenge, but it will be a hard-fought .

998ff12a26ed57ad.title: Three rebel AAP MLAs from Punjab join BJP ahead of Assembly polls
998ff12a26ed57ad.summary: In a setback to the Aam Aadmi Party ahead of the Punjab assembly polls, three of its leaders from the state, including Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh and two other legislators, joined the BJP on Monday. Earlier in the day, suspended AAP MLA and former IPS officer Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh said he resigned as a legislator of the Punjab Vidhan Sabha. In a post on Facebook, Singh -- the MLA from Amritsar North seat -- said he has sent his resignation to Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan. Singh, along with Punjab MLAs Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, joined the BJP in the presence of senior leaders at its headquarters here. His resignation from the Punjab Assembly came on the heels of two other AAP legislators -- Chetan Singh Jouramajra from Samana and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra from Sanour in Patiala district -- resigning from the party on Sunday.

af8f3d0c3943d793.title: Jagan accuses SEC of complicity in civic poll malpractices, says YSRCP will go to court
af8f3d0c3943d793.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:32 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy staging a protest outside the office of the Returning Officer in Pulivendula on Sunday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy has accused the State Election Commission (SEC) of being complicit in the electoral malpractices that took place during the urban local body elections on November 1. Instead of protecting democracy, the SEC acted as per the whims of the coalition government, he said. In an X post on Monday, Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy said the shocking incidents during the municipal elections, particularly those in Pulivendula, exposed how the SEC stood firmly behind the malpractices. The State Election Commission (SEC), which is meant to protect democracy, has become subservient to @ncbn. The shocking incidents during yesterday's municipal polling across the state, including in Pulivendula, show how the SEC is enabling election irregularities. Yesterday in Pulivendula, YSRCP agents were kept out of 70 of the 80 polling booths. TDP goons brought in from other areas went on a rampage with the support of election officials and the police. They attacked our party agents to stop them from entering polling booths. In some places, they dragged our agents out of the polling stations. These incidents took place with the police's support. Voter slips were snatched from people, polling booths were captured, and votes were rigged and cast repeatedly. The video evidence of these incidents is clear. Agents from all 70 booths came to me personally, showed their agent forms to the officials, lodged complaints and protested. The entire state witnessed what happened. Yet the SEC's response was shocking. Irregularities took place in 70 of the 80 booths, and our agents were attacked and forced out. In these circumstances, how was it fair for the SEC to order repolling in only four booths and then wash its hand

Flight services to and from Chennai, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam have been impacted. Chennai International Airport, in a post on social media platform X, said eleven flights have been cancelled to and from Chennai owing to the Cyclone. These historic markets house approximately 3,00,000 shops. Based on data we received this evening from various WhatsApp groups-comprising traders from different markets under the CTA (Confederation of All India Traders)-about 80% of these shops-roughly 2,50,000 out of 3,00,000-remained closed today," .

4576f06676c06a16.title: Suspended Punjab AAP leader Kunwar Vijay Pratap quits as MLA ahead of polls
4576f06676c06a16.summary: Amritsar North MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh announced his resignation, citing a push for clean politics and transparent administration | File Image: X@Kvijaypratap In a major political development ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, Amritsar North MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh announced his resignation from the Punjab Legislative Assembly on Monday. Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh was suspended from the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on June 29, 2025. In a X post addressed to the people of Amritsar, Singh said he would remain indebted to them "until my last breath" for their love and respect. He called for a collective effort to rise above "the politics of lanes and ribbon-cutting" and to bring Punjab, which he described as "trapped by drugs, extortion, gangsterism and corruption", back to being a progressive state. ਬਹੁਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਿਕਾਰਯੋਗ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ ਦੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਭੈਣ-ਭਰਾਵੋਂ, ਪੰਜਾਬ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਦੀ ਮੈਂਬਰਸ਼ਿਪ ਤੋਂ ਮੈਂ ਇਸਤੀਫ਼ਾ ਦੇ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਹੈ। ਮੈਂ ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਮਿਲੇ ਪਿਆਰ ਅਤੇ ਸਤਿਕਾਰ ਵਾਸਤੇ ਆਖ਼ਿਰੀ ਸਾਹ ਤੱਕ ਰਿਣੀ ਰਹਾਂਗਾ। >ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਸਹਿਯੋਗ ਅਤੇ ਪਰਮਾਤਮਾ ਦੇ ਆਸ਼ੀਰਵਾਦ ਨਾਲ ਗਲੀ-ਨਾਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਰਿਬਨ-ਕਟਿੰਗ ਦੀ ਰਾਜਨੀਤੀ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਪਰ ਉੱਠ ਕੇ ਨਸ਼ਾ, ਫਿਰੌਤੀ, ਗੈਂਗਸਟਰਵਾਦ ਅਤੇ ਭ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟਾਚਾਰ ਤੋਂ ਜਕੜੇ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਨੂੰ ਮੁੜ ਉੱਨਤਸ਼ੀਲ ਅਤੇ ਮੋਹਰੀ ਸੂਬਾ ਬਣਾਉਣ ਲਈ ਅਸੀਂ ਸਾਰਿਆਂ ਨੇ ਮਿਲ਼ ਕੇ ਇਕਜੁਟ ਪ੍ਰਯਾਸ ਕਰਨਾ ਹੈ। >ਵੈਸੇ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਸਾਰੇ ਜਾਣਦੇ ਹੋ ਕਿ ਮੈਂ ਬਤੌਰ ਵਿਧਾਇਕ ਆਪਣਾ 90 ਪਰਸੈਂਟ ਟਾਰਗੇਟ ਪੂਰਾ ਕਰ ਲਿਆ ਹੈ; ਜੋ ਕੰਮ ਇੱਕ ਵਿਧਾਇਕ ਨੇ ਕਰਨਾ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਕੌਂਸਲਰ, ਮੇਅਰ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਂਸਦ ਦੇ ਕੰਮ ਇਸਤੋਂ ਇਲਾਵਾ ਹਨ। >ਮੈਂ ਇਲਾਕਾ ਵਾਰ ਆਪਣੇ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਕਰਾਏ ਕੰਮਾਂ ਦਾ ਵੇਰਵਾ ਵੀ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਅਖ਼ਬਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਫੇਸਬੁੱਕ ਪੇਜ ਤੇ ਮੌਜੂਦ ਹੈ। >ਮੇਰੀ ਸੱਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡੀ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਮੈਂ ਰਾਜਨੀਤੀ ਤੋਂ ਮਾਈ-ਬਾਪ ਕਲਚਰ ਨੂੰ ਖਤਮ ਕੀਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਇੱਕ ਜਨਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣਾ ਪ੍ਰੇਰਣਾ-ਸਰੋਤ ਸਮਝ ਕੇ ਕੰਮ ਕੀਤਾ। >ਪੰਜਾਬ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਦੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੈਂ ਹਮੇਸ਼ਾ ਅੰਬਰਸਰੀਆਂ ਦੀ ਆਵਾਜ ਬੁਲੰਦ ਕੀਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਪਾਣੀ ਸੀਵਰੇਜ ਤੋਂ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਸਰਕਟ ਹਾਊਸ, ਕੰਪਨੀ ਬਾਗ, ਗੰਦਾ ਨਾਲਾ, ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀ, ਸਰਕਾਰੀ ਮੈਡੀਕਲ ਕਾਲਜ, ਸਰੂਪ ਰਾਣੀ ਕਾਲਜ ਅਤੇ ਬਰਗਾੜੀ ਬੇਅਦਬੀ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਦੇ ਬੇਬਾਕੀ ਨਾਲ ਰੱਖੇ। ਇਹ ਪਹਿਲੀ ਵਾਰ ਹੋਇਆ ਕਿ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਦੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਗਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਮੁਹੱਲਾ ਦਾ ਨਾਂ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਇਲਾਕੇ ਵਾਰ ਮੁੱਦੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਵਲੋਂ ਉਠਾਏ ਗਏ। >ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਕੇ ਅੱਗੇ ਦੀ ਸਟ੍

836fbbd76fe0e28f.title: Andhra goes ahead with Kotia local body polls despite Odisha’s plea in Supreme Court
836fbbd76fe0e28f.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:39 pm IST - PARVATIPURAM A resident of Madkar village in the Kotia gram panchayat shows voter cards issued by both the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha governments. Andhra Pradesh is going ahead with local body polls in the disputed villages on November 5. File | Photo Credit: Biswaranjan Rout The Andhra Pradesh government and the State Election Commission are making all arrangements to conduct local body elections in the Kotia group of villages on the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha border, despite strong objections from Odisha. The neighbouring State has approached the Supreme Court to stop the election process in the disputed region. Both the States have been at odds over the jurisdiction of the Kotia group of villages for about seven decades. Both have also been holding local body elections there for many decades. Odisha has objected before: it filed contempt petitions when Andhra Pradesh held polls in the villages in 2021. This time, it filed a fresh contempt petition last month, alleging that the poll notification violates the Supreme Court’s 2006 order directing both States to maintain the status quo. The villages are located 35 km from Salur town of Parvathipuram Manyam district. Since the court has not passed any order on Odisha’s petition, the Parvathipuram Manyam district administration is making all arrangements to hold elections in places like Ganjai Bhadra, Pagalu Chennuru, Pattu Chennuru, Kurukutti, Sarika, Kotia and other villages on November 5, 2026. The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which won the Salur Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency and all four Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies in 2021, is keen to win them again with its spirited campaign in all Kotia villages. 7ac472482663b212.title: Cyclone Murasu: Red alert in two Telangana districts, orange in three more on November 3
7ac472482663b212.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:21 pm IST - HYDERABAD Nagarkurnool and Nalgonda districts in Telangana were placed under red alert on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT With Cyclone Murasu likely to make landfall at Andhra Pradesh coast between evening of Monday (November 2, 2026) and early morning of Tuesday (November 3, 2026), the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for two Telangana districts and an orange alert in three districts for Tuesday (November 3, 2026). According to the IMDs latest bulletin, a red alert — meaning, heavy to very heavy rain with isolated extremely heavy rainfall — was issued for Nalgonda and Nagarkurnool districts. An orange alert — meaning heavy to very heavy rainfall — was issued for Suryapet, Mahabubnagar and Wanaparthy districts. Additionally, a yellow alert — indicating heavy rainfall with thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds — was issued for Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Mahabubabad, Warangal, Hanumakonda, Jangaon, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri, Rangareddy, Vikarabad, Narayanpet and Jogulamba Gadwal districts. Hyderabad city for the next 24 hours will see a generally cloudy sky. “Moderate to heavy rain or thundershowers by lightning accompanied with gusty winds are very likely to occur in parts of the city towards evening or night. f0f2e9e125ddf598.title: Shock and regret: scientists react to AI roiling life’s work
f0f2e9e125ddf598.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:42 pm IST For decades, three computer scientists built their careers around an idea about the limits of what computers can do. Artificial intelligence may now have shown it to be wrong: OpenAI and Anthropic each said last week that one of their AI models had disproved the exponential time hypothesis (ETH). The hypothesis holds that some problems are so hard that computers can solve them only by trying nearly every possible answer. Hundreds of studies in computer science and biology rely on it. The claim is the latest in a string of AI results that have shaken academia, setting off soul-searching, most notably among mathematicians, over the value of human expertise and the future of their profession. Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi of the University of California San Diego first proposed the hypothesis around 25 years ago. Ryan Williams of MIT, a leading researcher in the field, had long publicly doubted it. The three are now helping organise an independent review of the claims from the AI companies. Q: How did you feel when you learned that a machine may have overturned this hypothesis? Ryan Williams: I did not fully believe the hypothesis, and I’m on the record as a prominent sceptic. So I felt vindicated. Russell Impagliazzo: I’m afraid I am less cheerful about this than the others. I would have much preferred it to be discovered by a human who could explain their thought process. And I’d like to have shaken the (actual) hand of the person who disproved ETH. Q: What is left for human researchers facing the machine? What would you tell a student? Paturi: These breakthroughs extend the frontier of research, but I believe shaping that frontier and moving it forward remain within human capacity and creativity. I would encourage young students to join. They should learn to use these tools while developing their own judgment.
